Title: Melaka sanctuary's green anaconda gives birth to 10 after 7 months without food
Article:
AYER KEROH: A 2.74m-long green anaconda named Diana has given birth to 10 offspring at the Melaka Butterfly and Reptile Sanctuary after going nearly seven months without food.
The sanctuary's managing director, Gerard Wong, said Diana gave birth on Monday after a gestation period of about 190 days.
He said the birth marked a milestone in wildlife conservation, as the offspring represent the second generation of green anacondas bred at the sanctuary.
The births bring the sanctuary's green anaconda population to more than 40, making it home to Malaysia's largest population of the species.
"This is meaningful because Diana was born at the sanctuary in August 2020.
"This second generation proves conservation and breeding efforts involving exotic species native to South America can be carried out in Malaysia," he said at a press conference today.
Unlike most snakes, which lay eggs, green anacondas give birth to live young. They typically go without food throughout their gestation period, which lasts about six to seven months.
Wong said the birth demonstrated the sanctuary's expertise and facilities in breeding exotic reptiles.
He said breeding green anacondas, among the world's largest snake species, required meticulous care, particularly in maintaining suitable temperatures, water cleanliness and currents that mimic their natural habitat in the Amazon Basin.
"Besides serving as an educational attraction, Diana's breeding has given our team an opportunity to document and better understand the reproductive process of green anacondas," he said.
Wong said the sanctuary had also hatched 23 baby caimans, another reptile native to South America, including the Amazon Basin.
The sanctuary plans to organise a carnival soon to allow visitors and animal lovers to see the baby anacondas and caimans up close.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'We will not return': Imran Khan supporters march for his release
Article:
Punching the air and roaring in Unison, ecstatic crowds joined a growing demonstration on Wednesday in support of Pakistan's jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, an opposition show of force that authorities had sought to avert.
Supporters of Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party began their so-called "long march" on Sunday, demanding his release and airing anti-government sentiment fuelled by harsh economic conditions.
"I joined this procession for one reason: Imran Khan's release. I will not return under any circumstances until he is released," 58-year-old Qalandar Khan said in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, ruled by the PTI.
"If the government and the establishment think they can remove Imran Khan... they should know that he has a place in our hearts," said the protester from the mountainous North Waziristan area.
A hugely popular former cricket star, Imran has been behind bars since August 2023 and faces scores of charges from corruption to treason following anti-establishment riots also in 2023.
He and his legal team reject the allegations, branding them as politically motivated cases aimed at neutralising his popularity.
"Imran Khan wanted to establish peace in the country and eliminate corruption," said protester Pir Fayyaz, 40, a property dealer from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
"We have become deeply frustrated with inflation, lawlessness, poor governance and terrorism in the country," he added.
"We are Khan's soldiers," Sohail Afridi, PTI chief minister for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, shouted down a microphone as he addressed crowds south of Peshawar city, ahead of the fourth day of the march.
From atop a truck with a five-metre-high platform festooned with smiling pictures of the jailed former prime minister, Afridi reiterated PTI demands including access in prison to Imran for doctors, party officials and relatives.
Raising his fist in the air, Afridi asked the crowd: "Are you ready to march to Islamabad?"
The packed crowd of protesters, some holding red-and-green party flags or clutching pictures of Imran, cheered back: "We are ready."
A police intelligence official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said there were 1,500 vehicles and some 5,000 to 6,000 people travelling within the convoy in the PTI's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa stronghold.
With fears of potential violence, authorities have been preparing for weeks for the possible arrival of demonstrators in the capital Islamabad, with the march originally slated for Sept 27 and then postponed until Sunday.
On Tuesday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urged the PTI to call off the march and re-enter negotiations with the government. Talks between the two sides hit an impasse early Sunday before the march began.
The Pakistani premier also warned of the demonstration's negative impact on the economy, saying that undermining the government's efforts would be met with the force of law.
The march is yet to pass outside the confines of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, leaving open the possibility of an agreement between the opposition and the government to end the demonstration.
"We are not taking the law into our own hands," 40-year-old Bismillah Jan said from the march.
He added, however, that: "All party workers, including myself, are ready to make any sacrifice for Imran Khan."
The demonstration pressed to Khyber tribal district, with the PTI and Pakistan flags flying, music blaring from loudspeakers, and vehicles showered in flower petals.
Farmer Changiz Khan, 58, was dressed in the red and green colours of Khan's party.
"The country is currently experiencing a continued decline," he said. "We believe that after Imran Khan's release, the country will return to the path of development.
"We will continue the struggle until we achieve our objective and gain control over our own land."
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mercy Malaysia rolls out nationwide haze emergency response
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mercy Malaysia is rolling out its Haze Emergency Response nationwide to supply medical aid and health guidance to vulnerable groups as air quality worsens across several states.
In a statement today, the humanitarian organisation said the initiative builds on its ongoing efforts in Sarawak, where it has supported public health advocacy, community awareness and assistance for those affected by haze.
"Haze is currently affecting several parts of Peninsular Malaysia, including Johor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur. Severity varies from place to place, but the risk to vulnerable groups remains.
"Children, older persons, pregnant women and people with respiratory or heart conditions face the greatest health risks," it said.
With the Northeast Monsoon approaching, Mercy Malaysia is preparing for possible haze-related needs in western parts of the country and elsewhere by monitoring conditions, assessing emerging needs and coordinating with relevant stakeholders.
As part of its response, the organisation has prepared Haze Emergency Response Kits containing loratadine, wet wipes, normal saline, lozenges, a KF94 face mask, a small clear pouch and a health information flyer.
Mercy Malaysia urged federal and state authorities and relevant agencies to keep coordination strong, issue timely and clear public health advisories, support high-risk groups and speed up assistance to affected communities.
Mercy Malaysia president Datuk Dr Ahmad Faizal Mohd Perdaus said tackling haze required collective action involving government agencies, civil society, the private sector and the public.
"Haze is not something any one agency, community or individual can manage alone. It takes collective action as a nation," he said, urging the public to follow health advisories, protect their families, check on neighbours and support communities most affected.
He said cooperation among all parties was essential to ensure information, protection and assistance reached affected communities promptly.
Mercy Malaysia is appealing for public and corporate contributions to support the preparation and distribution of haze response kits, public health advocacy and assistance for affected communities. - BERNAMA

Title: Song Swee Guan's legacy and SUPP's unfinished comeback
Article:
Sarawak bade farewell to a towering political legend in the person of Datuk Song Swee Guan this week. He died of old age at 84 after a short hospital stay.
Song had served four terms as a state assemblyman representing Padungan in Kuching, now an opposition stronghold. In addition, he was Bandar Kuching member of parliament from 1995 to 2003.
A stalwart of the Sarawak United People's Party (SUPP), a component of the state ruling coalition, Song was probably best known for being the first mayor of Kuching South.
Through much of the 1980s, he had served as chairman of the then Kuching Municipal Council (KMC). When Kuching was elevated to city status in 1988, Song became its founding mayor.
He retired from politics after serving a term as speaker of the Sarawak Legislative Assembly.
A life-long bachelor and son of a long-serving KMC chairman, Song Thian Cheok, Song's political star was somewhat dimmed in later years when rather serious personal financial misfortune required the intervention of party leaders.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg has described Song as a humble and dedicated public servant.
"The late Tun Taib (Sarawak's chief minister who went on to become Yang Di-pertua Negeri) even recommended him (Song) to contest in Padungan and Bandar Kuching. And he won. That shows how strong his grassroots support was," Abang Johari noted.
Current Sarawak Legislative Assembly Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar, who had served as deputy to Song, noted that in Song, SUPP had a popular political figure who contested in Bandar Kuching against another political legend, the late Sim Kwang Yang of DAP.
"We had a strong DAP man and Song managed to defeat him. As such, he was the only one who became mayor, MP and state assembly speaker.
"He was also considered a popular hero," Asfia reminisced.
In that sense, Song represented a revival of political fortune for SUPP which had suffered setbacks after it became part of the state government in 1970, culminating in the defeat of then deputy chief minister Tan Sri Stephen Yong in a Kuching constituency in 1974.
After Song's triumph in Bandar Kuching, no other SUPP candidate has been able to wrest back Bandar Kuching from the DAP.
In Kuching, the Chinese-majority SUPP seems to face a classic Chinese-voter dilemma: how to be a consequential party in government while maintaining Chinese voters' desire for real political checks and balance.
The state assembly now has all of only two opposition members from DAP, who won at the expense of SUPP.
SUPP must hope that the revival it experienced after the late Tan Sri Adenan Satem became chief minister would undergo a further boost in the coming state election.
That revival was reinforced after Abang Johari took over from Adenan and won the last state election by a landslide.
The nostalgia kindled by all the public tributes generated following Song's demise may serve to further entrench SUPP's political comeback.
The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Police to strengthen operational capabilities, combat digital crime
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police will optimise the allocations under the 2027 Budget to strengthen operational readiness, enhance enforcement capabilities and address increasingly complex digital crime threats.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the force was committed to ensuring that every allocation was utilised efficiently and with integrity to improve the effectiveness of police service delivery.
He said they appreciated the RM22 billion allocation to the Home Ministry, including RM7.1 billion for the procurement and maintenance of security forces' assets.
The construction of the 19th General Operations Force (GOF) Battalion Complex in Cheras and three new police stations in Melaka, Perak and Sarawak are also expected to strengthen the force's infrastructure and operational capabilities.
In efforts to curb digital crime, Khalid welcomed the development of an artificial intelligence (AI) application by the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC), as well as the enhancement of the Malaysia Internet Crime Against Children system by the D11 division.
He said these initiatives could strengthen the prevention and early detection of online scams, while enhancing protection for children against the threat of sexual exploitation.
"Police also welcome the RM1.1 billion allocation to enhance the operational capabilities of enforcement agencies in addressing increasingly complex security challenges," he said in a statement.
In terms of welfare, he also welcomed the increase in the allocation to RM2.3 billion for the construction and maintenance of civil servants' quarters, which he believed would improve the well-being and motivation of police personnel.
Khalid also welcomed welfare measures for civil servants and retirees, including special financial assistance of RM1,500 for civil servants and RM750 for retirees, improved ex-gratia waris pukal benefits and a minimum monthly pension increase to RM1,350.
He also welcomed the initiative to provide special promotion opportunities under the Khas Untuk Penyandang (KUP) scheme to 12,000 officers in the management and professional Group, as well as improvements relating to maternity leave and an increase in allowances for police volunteers.

Title: NST Leader: The haze crisis needs more than promises
Article:
With schools in half of the country ordered closed in view of the worsening haze, the command by the king to prioritise the health of schoolchildren is well taken.
The sudden school closures as pollution readings inch towards highly "unhealthy" levels are more than just a health emergency.
It has also disrupted the lives of parents who must find guardians for their children while they are at work. It is natural for Malaysians to blame Indonesia, where the forest fires—often deliberately set—originate.
More so when this has been a recurring problem during the dry season for more than two decades.
We wonder how many more school closures, disrupted flights, hospital admissions and weeks of inhaling unhealthy air will it take before the haze is treated as a standing regional emergency rather than a seasonal inconvenience.
Malaysia has rightly sought Indonesia's cooperation. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has spoken to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, who assured him that necessary steps are being taken.
Malaysia's offer to assist in putting out the fires has been accepted by Indonesia but protocols must be streamlined so precious time is not wasted before joint action begins.
Public fury in Malaysia over the haze is understandable but must be tempered with empathy for Indonesians in southern Sumatra and Kalimantan, who are suffering from even worse chocking conditions.
If anything, the fury of Indonesians over their authorities' lacklustre response to the fires and culprits must be growing.
Our hope is that Indonesians themselves will demand an end to this haze pollution once and for all. Assurances from the top Indonesian leadership, however welcome, cannot be the endpoint.
The recurring nature of transboundary haze demands concrete action, accountability and prevention, rather than crisis management every time the skies turn grey due to man-made causes.
That said, instead of turning public fury over the haze into a diplomatic confrontation with Indonesia, it is far more fruitful to welcome Prabowo's commitment to get to the root of the problem and work together for mutually beneficial end results.
However, Malaysia must make clear that good neighbourliness does not mean accepting the same crisis year after year.
Indonesia needs to demonstrate that its assurances translate into real, long-lasting effective action on the ground.
Malaysia and Asean as a whole, meanwhile, need to work to strengthen the mechanisms to prevent another haze episode ever becoming a region-wide public health crisis again.
School closures should serve as a wake-up call. Children should not have to stay home because governments fail to prevent a problem that has been recurring for decades.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians in Saudi Arabia advised to avoid high-risk areas amid security tensions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh has advised Malaysians in Saudi Arabia to stay calm and follow official safety directives following recent security developments in the Gulf country.
"Malaysians are advised to avoid high-risk areas and refrain from taking or sharing any photographs or videos related to current security incidents that could cause panic or disrupt the operations of the authorities," the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh said in a statement posted on its Facebook page.
Malaysians have been advised to plan their journeys carefully and check flight statuses directly with airlines and airport authorities before travelling.
"The embassy remains in contact with the Saudi Arabian authorities and will communicate any significant developments requiring the attention of Malaysians through official channels," the statement said.
It advised Malaysians residing in or visiting Saudi Arabia to register and update their whereabouts to facilitate the dissemination of information and consular assistance, if necessary.
Malaysians requiring emergency consular assistance can contact the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh via its hotline at +966 56 300 6319 (emergencies only) or email mwriyadh@kln.gov.my. - BERNAMA

Title: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for career defending international law
Article:
OSLO: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded Friday to South Africa's Navi Pillay, the judge who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal and presided over a UN commission which accused Israel of genocide in Gaza – a move angrily denounced by Israel.
The 85-year-old, who is currently a judge on the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in a case in which Myanmar also stands accused of genocide, has spent her career defending international law.
She dedicated her award to the "survivors of international crimes", speaking Friday from the courtroom in Nuremberg, Germany where the trials prosecuting World War II Nazi leaders took place.
Pillay has been "instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide are prosecuted," said Jorgen Watne Frydnes, the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo.
Israel's foreign ministry said the award legitimised "anti-Israel hatred", and that Nazi propagandist Joseph Goebbels must be "applauding from hell."
The daughter of a bus driver in a family of Tamil descent, Pillay's career has taken her from South African courts, where she defended anti-apartheid activists, to the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court (ICC).
She headed the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza.
Pillay told AFP at the time that her team had shared "thousands of pieces of information" with prosecutors at the International Criminal Court.
Israel had categorically rejected the report's findings, slamming it as "distorted and false."
Pillay's "independence, her expertise and steadfastness have made her one of the most respected international jurists of our time," the Nobel committee said.
In Nuremberg, Pillay said world leaders have a "legal obligation to protect human rights and refrain from war", and criticised attacks on the ICC.
"We are living through an era when international law and human rights are under significant political attack," she said.
"This worsening reality is particularly visible with the attacks on the International Criminal Court," she continued.
US President Donald Trump last month called for all ICC member states to quit the body, denouncing it as a "rogue institution."
Earlier, she reacted to the news about her prize by making a quip about Trump's well-documented desire to win the prize himself.
"If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," Pillay said earlier during a standing ovation captured on video by Amnesty International Secretary General Agnes Callamard in Nuremberg and posted on the social network X.
- 'COURAGE TO SPEAK THE TRUTH' -
The Nobel committee said that while its prize honoured Pillay's career of fighting genocide, it was not taking a stand on whether Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a genocide.
Pillay noted that many had paid tribute to her courage in that report.
"You can imagine how surprised I was. Why would you need courage to speak the truth?"
The UN said her prize was a "testament to the need and to the value of human rights in this world more than ever", while the ICC said her award was of "particular significance" given the attacks on international law.
The prize for Pillay is sure to anger Trump, whose administration has repeatedly attacked international justice institutions.
"This is a clear message to those who are putting pressure on these institutions, to those who are sanctioning the judges and are attacking the institutions. That needs to stop," Frydnes told AFP after the announcement.
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prize, insisting that he was the most deserving candidate and claiming to have ended up to eight wars.
But his war against Iran, his territorial expansion ambitions as in Greenland, his hard line on migrants, and his attacks on multilateralism and the media have, according to experts in Oslo, disqualified him for the prize.
The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of US$1.2 million.
The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of the prize's creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prosecutors drop bribery charge in Philippine VP impeachment trial
Article:
MANILA: Prosecutors said Friday they are dropping a bribery charge against Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte, who still faces three other charges at her ongoing impeachment trial that could lead to her removal from office.
The 48-year-old is also charged with misuse of state funds, unexplained wealth, and an alleged assassination threat against one-time ally President Ferdinand Marcos.
If the Senate finds her guilty on any of the charges, she will be stripped of the vice presidency and permanently barred from elected office, ending her bid to become president in 2028.
Prosecutors from the House of Representatives, which voted to impeach Duterte in May, said the decision to drop the bribery charge would speed up the trial, which hit its 37th day Friday.
"We think we have presented enough (evidence). To drag it further might be stretching the patience not only of the people but also the senator-judges," Congressman and prosecutor Jonathan Keith Flores told reporters.
Prosecutors have already presented evidence and witnesses in support of the assassination and misuse of funds charges.
On Friday, prosecutor Jose Manuel Diokno told the court they had presented their last witness in the hidden wealth case. That witness will be cross-examined on Monday.
The Senate had originally given prosecutors 60 trial days to present their case, after which Duterte will present her own witnesses and evidence.
Last month, in a ruling widely seen as a blow to Duterte, the 24-seat Senate approved a lower threshold of votes needed to find her guilty, potentially making it easier to execute her ouster.
With at least four senators loyal to the vice president now absent from the trial – two in jail, another in hiding and a fourth on extended medical furlough abroad – only 14 votes are needed to find her guilty.
Senators voted that the constitutionally required two-thirds guilty verdict by "all members of the Senate" referred only to those "capable of participating."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai queen flies Gripen fighter jet solo for the first time
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand's Queen Suthida has flown a Gripen fighter jet solo for the first time, the royal household revealed Friday, watched on by her husband King Maha Vajiralongkorn, himself a keen pilot.
The 48-year-old queen took off in a single-seat JAS 39C from a military air base in southern Surat Thani province on Thursday, according to footage released by the royal household.
The outing followed weeks of simulator training at the base and about 10 hours in a two-seat Gripen, media reports said.
A former Thai Airways flight attendant who married the king in 2019, days before his coronation, Suthida began flying in 2010 and has logged nearly 1,190 hours.
She regularly flies as co-pilot to the king on royal trips, including landing at Bhutan's notoriously difficult Paro airport, the reports said.
Thailand already operates a squadron of Gripen C/D fighters made by Sweden's Saab, and last year signed a deal for three Gripen E jets and one Gripen F worth around US$556 million, with deliveries due by 2030.
After she landed, the king handed the queen a bouquet and pinned a Golden Gripen Order patch on her left arm, which reports said made her Thailand's first female Gripen pilot.--AFp
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil servants ready to implement 2027 Budget swiftly - Shamsul Azri
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar is confident civil servants are ready to ensure government policies, including  2027 Budget, are implemented swiftly and effectively.
He said the commitment of all civil servants was crucial to ensuring that the people could share the benefits of economic growth.
"For all civil servants, I am confident that we are always ready to shoulder these trusts and responsibilities as a National Covenant and continue to support government policies through swift and effective implementation, to ensure that the extraordinary benefits of economic growth can be felt by all," he said in a statement today.
Shamsul Azri also expressed his appreciation to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, for tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Themed "Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values", the budget allocates RM459.8 billion, comprising RM376.8 billion for operating expenditure and RM83 billion for development expenditure, based on eight key priorities.
The measures announced included raising the minimum wage to RM2,000, various tax incentives and exemptions, as well as subsidies, assistance and incentives totalling RM80 billion.
The budget also provides for Special Financial Assistance of RM1,500 for civil servants and RM750 for government retirees.
Shamsul Azri said the 2027 Budget reflected the government's commitment to continuing to prioritise the welfare of the people while balancing national development, economic sustainability and fiscal resilience.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Don't leave contract pharmacists behind, govt told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's move to offer permanent positions to more than 9,000 contract doctors under the 2027 Budget has prompted calls for similar clarity on the future of contract pharmacists, who continue to face employment uncertainty.
The Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) said contract pharmacists should not be overlooked in efforts to address longstanding job insecurity in the public healthcare sector.
Its president, Professor Amrahi Buang, welcomed the government's announcement but said pharmacists who had served for years in public hospitals, health clinics and other Health Ministry facilities also deserved a clear pathway to permanent employment.
"Pharmacists who have committed years of service to the public healthcare system deserve a transparent, fair and sustainable pathway towards long-term employment.
"A solution to the contract healthcare workforce issue cannot be considered complete if pharmacists facing the same employment uncertainty are left without a clear pathway forward.
"This is not a call for preferential treatment. It is a call for fairness, transparency and appropriate recognition of every healthcare profession that contributes to the delivery of public healthcare," he said in a statement today.
Amrahi said many contract pharmacists continued to face uncertainty over permanent appointments, career progression and their long-term future, despite playing essential roles in medication management, clinical pharmacy services, medication safety and antimicrobial stewardship.
He called on the government and Health Ministry to clarify their plans for contract pharmacists, including those still serving, those on reserve lists and those who had completed their contractual service.
MPS also called for a transparent timeline and mechanism for permanent appointments, alongside meaningful engagement with the profession to determine the ministry's long-term pharmacy workforce requirements.
Amrahi acknowledged that workforce requirements and appointment mechanisms differed between healthcare professions, but said this should not leave contract pharmacists without clarity over their future indefinitely.
When tabling the 2027 Budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that
more than 9,000 contract doctors
would be offered permanent positions next year. This follows the appointment of more than 15,000 contract doctors to permanent positions since 2023, including 4,000 this year.
Anwar also announced that the monthly post-basic incentive for 47,000 paramedics and nurses would increase from RM100 to RM200. The Health Ministry's allocation will rise to RM47.7 billion next year, from RM46.5 billion this year.

Title: Thai court dismisses detention challenge by Chinese reporter
Article:
BANGKOK: A Thai court on Friday dismissed a challenge by a Chinese investigative journalist over his prolonged detention in Bangkok, a day after authorities began proceedings to extradite him to China, his lawyer said.
Bai Zhaodong, who is recognised by the United Nations as a refugee, left China in 2023 and arrived the following year in Thailand.
The 56-year-old had been detained at a Bangkok immigration centre since January, and he earlier filed a petition against what he said was unlawful detention by Thai immigration authorities.
On Thursday, Thai prosecutors arrested Bai under an extradition warrant issued by Beijing and moved him to a remand prison.
At a hearing on Friday morning, which was scheduled weeks earlier, Bangkok South Criminal Court rejected Bai's challenge against his detention, according to his lawyer.
"Because there is an extradition request from China saying he is wanted in China, the (court ruled that) detention is necessary," Nadthasiri Bergman told AFP.
Bai was not in court on Friday but is expected to appear at a Jan 25 hearing in the extradition case.
China's foreign ministry said in July that Bai was suspected of extortion and bribery, and an extradition request had been submitted to Thailand.
Bergman said the Chinese embassy in Bangkok sent a letter to the Thai Immigration Office in June 2025 asking to extradite Bai, while an official request dated March 4,  was sent to the Office of the Attorney General.
Rights campaigners believe Bai's life could be at risk if he is returned to China, saying he faced growing persecution over two decades of work exposing government corruption.
An undisclosed third country has offered Bai asylum but two attempts to travel there were cancelled this year after Thai immigration authorities withheld exit clearance without explanation, his legal team says.
Reporters Without Borders has called his treatment "scandalous" while Maya Wang, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch, said the move to extradite Bai was "deeply troubling."
"Thailand should not succumb to pressure from Beijing to extradite Bai based on trumped up charges," she said.
- HAVEN FOR FUGITIVES -
Beijing has long sought to clamp down on dissidents overseas, and campaigners accuse authorities in Thailand – where several notable activists have moved over the years – of complicity.
Thailand is not a party to the UN Refugee Convention, but is bound by the international legal principle of non-refoulement, which bars countries from sending people back to places where their lives or freedom are in danger.
Nonetheless Bangkok deported 40 Uyghurs to China in February last year over the objections of activists, who said the men could be tortured or mistreated.
The Thai foreign ministry did not respond to an AFP request for comment.
Questioned by AFP at a regular briefing Friday, Chinese foreign affairs ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning urged all countries to cooperate in "eliminating lawless areas and safe havens for fugitives."
"China's judicial organs handle cases in strict accordance with the law, carry out law enforcement and judicial cooperation with relevant countries in accordance with the law and agreements, and fully safeguard the lawful rights of relevant parties," she said.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Egyptian president El-Sisi arrives for 2-day state visit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi arrived at the Bunga Raya Complex at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) about 6.20pm today to begin a 2-day state visit to Malaysia.
He was received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
El-Sisi is visiting Malaysia at the invitation of Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim.
In a Facebook post, Anwar welcomed El-Sisi and said he had headed to the Bunga Raya Complex after tabling the 2027 Budget to receive the Egyptian president.
"Tomorrow, we will hold a bilateral meeting to assess progress in our cooperation and exchange views on regional and international issues, besides witnessing the exchange of several memorandums of understanding between Malaysia and Egypt," he said.
The visit is El-Sisi's first to Malaysia since he became Egypt's president in June 2014.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Plantations Ministry to study cooperation with Indonesia to prevent Kalimantan fires
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Plantation and Commodities Ministry will study a proposal to strengthen cooperation with Indonesia to prevent and control forest and land fires, including through the Council of Palm Oil Producing Countries (CPOPC).
The ministry said the cooperation could include information sharing and efforts to prevent and control fires in Kalimantan, following reports linking Malaysian plantation companies to forest and land fires in Indonesia.
It viewed reports by Greenpeace and Pantau Gambut on the matter seriously, including concerns over the impact on public health and the environment.
"Through the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), the ministry held an engagement session with six Malaysian companies on Sept 10 to obtain information on the fire situation and the preventive and control measures in place in their respective operating areas," it said in a statement.
It added that regular feedback was also obtained to monitor developments.
On reports linking PT Menteng Jaya Sawit Perdana (PT MJSP), a subsidiary of Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK), to the fires, the ministry said it had taken note of KLK's official explanation dated Oct 6.
KLK said PT MJSP adhered to a zero-burning policy and did not undertake replanting activities. It also said most of the fires originated outside its concession areas and outlined the prevention and control measures it had implemented.
The ministry said Malaysian companies operating overseas must comply with the laws of their host countries and implement effective fire prevention and control measures, including addressing the risk of fires spreading from surrounding areas.
MPOB, it said, would continue to monitor developments and obtain the latest information from Malaysian companies operating in Kalimantan.
It reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring the palm oil industry operates sustainably and responsibly, with public health and environmental protection as priorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two women burnt to death in Myvi-lorry collision in Yong Peng
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Two 22-year-old women were burnt to death when their car caught fire after colliding with a lorry at Batu 1, Jalan Yong Peng-Ayer Hitam, this afternoon.
The victims were identified as Perodua Myvi driver Siti Nur Batrisya Mohd Khalid and her front-seat passenger, Siti Nurmaisarah Abd Jalil.
Ayer Hitam Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Shamin Mohamed Salikin said the station received an emergency call at 4.21pm, and a team arrived at the scene four minutes later.
He said firefighters found the car about 80 per cent burnt, with both victims trapped in the driver's seat and front passenger seat.
"The team carried out firefighting operations before extricating both victims using special equipment. They were pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry medical officers," he said in a statement today.
Shamin said both victims were burnt beyond recognition. The three men in their 30s who were in the Isuzu lorry were uninjured.
The operation involved 16 personnel from the Ayer Hitam and Yong Peng fire and rescue stations and ended at 6.38pm. The bodies were handed over to the police for further action.

Title: 2027 Budget: MCMC steps up connectivity, digital safety and AI initiatives
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget, tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in the Dewan Rakyat today, outlines several government initiatives to strengthen the country's digital infrastructure through programmes implemented by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
Anwar said MCMC will step up efforts to improve internet connectivity, strengthen digital safety and accelerate artificial intelligence (AI) adoption under the 2027 Budget, backed by a RM5 billion allocation for the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela), which includes plans to extend 4G coverage to all Orang Asli villages next year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said WiFi coverage had been provided at all public university campuses, while 4G coverage had been extended to all Felda settlements.
"We have so far successfully provided WiFi coverage at all public university campuses and 4G coverage in all Felda settlements," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget.
He said efforts next year would focus on ensuring internet connectivity along 7,000km of roads and 1,700km of railway lines, as well as implementing the Madani Submarine Cable (SALAM) project.
The government will also work to extend 4G coverage to all Orang Asli villages, bringing more remote communities into the digital network.
The connectivity push forms part of the government's broader efforts to ensure Malaysians can benefit from digital services, education and economic opportunities, alongside initiatives to strengthen online protection and develop the country's digital capabilities.
A key priority is protecting the public from online scams and other cyber threats.
MCMC has blocked more than 5.7 billion scam-related calls and short message service messages, while the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) will develop an AI-powered application to help the public check suspicious phone numbers, bank accounts and links.
The initiative aims to help people identify potential scams before falling victim to them.
Efforts to protect children online will also be strengthened. The police's D11 division will enhance the Malaysia Internet Crime Against Children (MICAC) system with advanced analytics, while MCMC will intensify its Safer Internet Campaign in schools nationwide, focusing on cyberbullying and child exploitation.
Beyond digital safety, the government is looking to accelerate AI adoption, develop local expertise and strengthen the country's digital capabilities.
An additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions will be made available, including access to applications such as ChatGPT, to widen access to AI tools.
The government is also developing a sovereign AI cloud, while RM6 billion has been allocated for research and development and commercialisation across ministries.
AI Malaysia Bhd will receive nearly RM15 million to strengthen the safe and ethical AI ecosystem, supporting the country's target of producing 200,000 skilled AI workers.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Digital Economy Corporation will receive RM30 million to help 4,000 micro, small and medium enterprises adopt AI and automate their operations. A separate programme will train and certify 5,000 AI professionals.
To prepare for emerging cybersecurity risks, the National Cyber Security Agency and MCMC will develop local data protection technologies to address post-quantum threats and strengthen CSCDC Bhd.
The government is also investing in digital skills and entrepreneurship to help more Malaysians participate in the digital economy.
The Digital Rakyat platform offers more than 16,000 courses and certificates through Coursera, providing users with opportunities to acquire new skills and improve their employability.
At the community level, RM142 million has been allocated to strengthen the NADI platform, which helps people in underserved areas access digital services and develop online businesses.
The platform has also helped entrepreneurs expand their reach. One example is Azmi Warisan, an entrepreneur from Kampung Sungai Leman, Selangor, whose sales increased by 80 per cent to RM240,000 through Nadi.
The allocation is expected to further support digital entrepreneurship and help communities participate more actively in the digital economy.
MCMC's role will also extend to healthcare, where digitalisation is expected to improve service delivery and efficiency.
The commission will continue implementing the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) System at healthcare facilities nationwide through the National Digital Health Ecosystem and Connectivity Driver (PERSADA) initiative, with an investment of RM1 billion.
The initiative is expected to improve the efficiency of healthcare service delivery to the public.
Other healthcare measures announced under the 2027 Budget include the MediAsas basic medical plan, scheduled to be introduced in January 2027.
Under the plan, hospital charges will be based on diagnosis and treatment. Employees Provident Fund members below 55 may pay premiums using savings in Akaun Sejahtera.
Employees of small and medium enterprises will also receive a RM200 subsidy towards the first-year premium. The scheme is open to SMEs with fewer than 75 employees, with the subsidy capped at 50 employees per company. It is expected to benefit up to 200,000 workers.
In a move to improve transparency, private hospital bills will adopt standardised charge categories from 2027. The e-CKAPS portal will also digitise the licensing process for private healthcare facilities, with processing times expected to be reduced by up to 65 per cent.
Taken together, the initiatives place digital technology at the centre of the government's efforts to improve connectivity, protect the public, support businesses, widen access to skills and improve essential services.

Title: Singapore prepares to distribute N95 masks as haze nears 'very unhealthy' levels
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore said on Friday it was "ready to roll out" a haze pollution action plan that included the distribution of masks, as air quality dipped towards "very unhealthy" levels.
The city-state was regarded as the "most polluted global major city" early Friday, according to a Swiss-based air quality monitor, as toxic haze from fires in neighbouring Indonesia continued to drive up air pollution levels.
"Based on the current situation it is possible" that air quality levels "may enter the very unhealthy range," Singapore's National Environmental Agency said in a statement.
The NEA and other agencies "stand ready to roll out the next tier of action plans and advisories to protect the health and well-being of the public," it said.
It said the government has set aside haze-rated masks and if pollution levels dipped into very unhealthy levels, "grassroots organisations will start distributing N95 masks to eligible Singaporeans."
"To complement... distribution, mask vending machines will also be made available at selected public transport hubs and social services offices," the NEA added.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM935mil tourism allocation offers opportunities for Sabah, says Jafry
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is looking to strengthen its tourism sector through improved international connectivity, destination promotion and conservation following the tabling of the 2027 Budget.
State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the RM935 million allocated for tourism and culture nationwide would create opportunities for Sabah to promote its destinations, develop tourism products and preserve its cultural heritage ahead of Visit Sabah 2027.
"Sabah welcomes the emphasis placed on the tourism sector, particularly efforts to improve facilities, strengthen promotion and expand international flight connectivity.
"These measures are in line with our efforts to increase tourist arrivals, encourage longer stays and ensure that the economic benefits of tourism reach more Sabahans," he said in a statement.
Jafry described the matching grants for international and charter flights as a strategic measure to strengthen Sabah's air links with key markets, including China, India, Central Asia and Europe.
He said better air connectivity was crucial to improving Sabah's competitiveness as an international destination while creating opportunities for the local tourism industry.
On conservation, he welcomed the attention given to Danum Valley, which has been identified as a potential heritage site for facility improvements and Unesco recognition.
"Tourism development and environmental conservation must go hand in hand.
"Sabah's biodiversity treasures are invaluable assets that must continue to be protected through a responsible development approach," he said.
Jafry added that improvements to road networks and basic infrastructure were essential to expanding access to rural tourism destinations and stimulating economic activity among local communities.
"Our priority is not merely to bring more tourists to Sabah, but to ensure they explore more destinations, stay longer and deliver direct benefits to local communities.
"The Tourism, Culture and Environment Ministry will continue to work closely with federal ministries and agencies to leverage the initiatives under Budget 2027 to strengthen Sabah's position as a competitive and sustainable international tourism destination," he said.

Title: 2027 Budget: Here are the key announcements [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today tabled the fifth Madani Budget in the Dewan Rakyat, reaffirming the government's commitment to ensuring national progress benefits every Malaysian through improved living standards, protected livelihoods and the opportunity to live with dignity.
The expansionary fiscal policy mobilises RM510 billion in overall national resources, up from RM470 billion previously.
The breakdown is as follows:
* RM376.8 billion in federal operating expenditure;
* RM83 billion in federal development expenditure;
* RM25 billion in investments by government-linked investment companies (GLICs);
* RM11 billion in public-private investments; and
* RM14.2 billion in investments by federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated companies.
FOR THE PEOPLE
1. Minimum wage increased to RM2,000
The minimum wage will rise from RM1,700 to RM2,000, effective June 2027. Micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales below RM50 million are exempted.
2. RM2,500 minimum wage for semi-skilled workers and graduates
A minimum wage of RM2,500 for semi-skilled workers and graduates will be introduced as the first step towards reforming the workers' income framework. No implementation date was announced.
3. Living wage benchmark raised to RM3,400
The living wage benchmark for GLICs and government-linked companies (GLCs) will rise from RM3,100 to RM3,400 a month, benefiting 230,000 workers.
4. Individual income tax relief increased to RM12,000
The individual income tax relief will increase from RM9,000 to RM12,000.
5. Tax rates reduced for two income brackets
* Taxable income of RM70,000 to RM100,000: 18 per cent.
* Taxable income of RM100,000 to RM150,000: 24 per cent.
6. Expanded individual tax reliefs
Tax reliefs will cover postnatal care, care for parents and grandparents, sports shoes, children's tuition, AI subscriptions, vaccinations and the adoption of pets from registered centres.
7. RM16 billion for STR and Sara assistance
The government will allocate RM16 billion for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara). STR recipients will receive Sara assistance of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year.
8. Non-STR recipients to receive Sara assistance twice
Malaysians aged 18 and above who do not receive STR will receive RM100 in Sara assistance ahead of Hari Raya Aidilfitri and in conjunction with the country's 70th Independence Day celebrations.
9. Sara can be used to buy fresh produce at markets
Sara recipients can use the assistance to purchase fresh produce at 216 farmers' markets and tamu markets under the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama).
10. RM160 million package for gig workers
The government and Grab will fund a package covering minimum income, maintenance, insurance and Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributions, starting in 2027.
11. Matching contributions for gig workers
* Socso: Government contributions of 35 per cent, rising to 50 per cent if the platform also contributes.
* Employees Provident Fund (EPF): Contributions of up to RM600 a year, or RM6,000 over a lifetime, for e-hailing and p-hailing drivers.
12. Automatic EPF registration at age 18
Every Malaysian citizen will be registered as an EPF member. The announcement did not state that registration would include automatic monetary contributions.
13. Proposed stamp duty exemption for first-time homebuyers
Full exemption will be given for homes priced up to RM500,000.
For homes priced up to RM750,000, the first RM500,000 will be fully exempt, with a 50 per cent exemption on the remaining amount.
The sale and purchase agreement must be signed between Jan 1, 2027, and Dec 31, 2030.
14. RM20 billion in housing financing guarantees
The Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) aims to assist 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly self-employed individuals without fixed incomes.
15. Early Schooling Assistance increased to RM200
The assistance will rise from RM150 to RM200 per student for the 2027 school session.
16. PTPTN repayment concessions
* Repayment deferment for borrowers earning up to RM2,500 a month.
* Minimum repayment of RM50 a month for those earning between RM2,500 and RM3,000.
* A 10 per cent discount for borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments.
17. FLYSiswa assistance increased to RM500
The assistance will rise from RM400 to RM500, benefiting more than 60,000 students at public institutions of higher learning.
18. MYKOMUTER50 introduced
The new initiative will benefit KTM Komuter users. The existing My50 pass will continue.
19. MediAsas to be introduced in January 2027
EPF members below 55 can pay premiums through their Sejahtera Account. Specific premium rates have not been announced.
20. Increased assistance for persons with disabilities and special education
* Assistance for the care of bedridden persons with disabilities and chronically ill patients: RM600 a month.
* Special education student allowance: RM200 a month.
* Eligibility income threshold for the Disabled Workers Allowance raised to RM2,000.
21. Bankruptcy threshold raised to RM150,000
The threshold will increase from RM100,000 to RM150,000, effective 2027.
22. Disaster victims' home repair assistance doubled to RM10,000
The assistance will rise from RM5,000 to RM10,000.
23. Permanent positions for more than 9,000 contract doctors
More than 9,000 contract doctors will be offered permanent positions in 2027.
FOR BUSINESSES
24. MSME tax rates reduced
* First RM150,000 in taxable income: 14 per cent.
* Taxable income between RM150,000 and RM600,000: 16 per cent.
Each eligible MSME is estimated to benefit by up to RM6,000.
25. RM6.6 billion in microfinancing
The allocation includes RM3 billion for Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM), RM1.3 billion for Tekun Nasional and RM1.7 billion for Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN).
26. RM200 million for Madani Sejahtera Grant
The grant will fund equipment and training for 40,000 recipients, particularly women.
27. Additional RM5 billion in Bank Negara financing
The financing will assist small and medium enterprises (SMEs) affected by the West Asia conflict.
28. DBKL premises rental reduced by 50 per cent
The reduction will apply throughout 2027, benefiting more than 10,000 small traders.
29. RM7.5 billion in procurement for Bumiputera G1–G4 contractors
The allocation will increase from RM4 billion.
For maintenance, repair and upgrading works at government facilities, direct appointments will be allowed for contracts worth up to RM200,000, while quotations will apply for contracts worth up to RM3 million.
30. Variation of Price clauses reintroduced
Variation of Price (VOP) clauses will be reintroduced specifically to cover increases in diesel and bitumen costs.
31. Matching grants of up to RM5,000 for halal certification
The grants will support MSMEs obtaining halal certification for the first time.
32. MediAsas premium subsidies for SME employees
A subsidy of RM200 per employee will be provided for the first year. For SMEs with fewer than 75 employees, the subsidy is capped at 50 employees per company.
33. Investment and financing incentives
* Certain accelerated capital allowances extended until the end of 2030.
* Stamp duty on peer-to-peer (P2P) financing reduced to RM10 for the 2027–2030 period.
* Green technology incentives, offering Investment Tax Allowances of up to 100 per cent, extended until the end of 2030.
34. Tax deductions for employers paying employees' PTPTN loans
The deductions will apply to payments made between Jan 1, 2027, and Dec 31, 2028.
FOR PADDY FARMERS AND SMALLHOLDERS
35. Paddy harvesting incentive increased to RM100
The incentive will rise from RM50 to RM100 per hectare per season. The RM300 ploughing incentive will be maintained and extended to Sabah and Sarawak.
36. RM100 million in hybrid financing for oil palm replanting
The financing will benefit 4,500 smallholders, with only half of the amount requiring repayment.
37. Rubber Production Incentive increased to RM3.30 per kg
The rate will rise from RM3 to RM3.30 per kg, benefiting more than 300,000 smallholders.
FOR THE PEOPLE AND CIVIL SERVANTS
38. RM1,000 assistance for taxi and school bus drivers
A one-off payment will be given to 38,000 taxi drivers, including rental car drivers, and 15,000 school bus drivers. Payments will be disbursed in the week following the Budget presentation.
39. Minimum pension increased to RM1,350
The minimum pension will rise from RM1,000 to RM1,350 a month, benefiting nearly 59,000 pensioners, Malaysian Armed Forces veterans and derivative pension recipients.
40. Improved maternity leave for civil servants
Lifetime maternity leave entitlement will increase from 360 to 490 days, with a maximum of 98 days per birth.
41. Special promotions for 12,000 officers
A one-off Khas Untuk Penyandang (KUP) promotion will be offered to outstanding officers in the Management and Professional group who face promotion constraints due to limited established posts.
42. Allowances for volunteer personnel increased
* RM9 an hour for personnel.
* RM10.80 an hour for supervisors.
The increase covers the People's Volunteer Corps (Rela), Auxiliary Fire and Rescue personnel, Police Volunteers and Civil Defence Volunteers.
43. Ex-gratia lump-sum benefits for dependants increased to RM50,000
The benefit will rise from RM20,000, subject to length of service, for deaths resulting from accidents related to workplace disasters. The measure takes effect on Jan 1, 2026.
44. Additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions
The subscriptions will be made available to young people, with access extended to new applications such as ChatGPT.
45. Free access to more than 16,000 digital courses
The courses will be available through the Rakyat Digital platform in collaboration with Coursera, including Professional Certificate programmes.
46. Budi Belia: RM100 e-wallet incentive
The incentive will be given to young people who complete a specified number of volunteer hours with selected non-governmental organisations. Detailed requirements and the required number of hours have not been announced.
47. Bakat Madani targets 30,000 new job opportunities
The initiative aims to create 30,000 new job opportunities in 2027, including through private-sector participation.
48. Three million skills training opportunities
The Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) will provide RM3 billion in funding, while the Skills Development Fund Corporation (PTPK) will provide RM500 million in financing for trainees at registered institutions.
49. Mitra allocation increased to RM150 million
The allocation will prioritise training and employment opportunities for Indian youths, including in industrial automation, technology and aircraft maintenance.
50. Rukun Tetangga grants increased to RM10,000 a year
Annual grants for each active registered neighbourhood watch area will increase from RM6,000 to RM10,000.
51. Full Socso contributions for mosque personnel to be covered
Through Tabung Haji, the contributions will cover 40,000 imams, bilals, mosque caretakers, mosque attendants and guru takmir (religious instructors).
52. Special allowance of RM150 a month for Kafa teachers
The allowance will benefit 500 teachers educating students with special needs under the Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain (Kafa) programme.
53. Duty-free purchase limit raised to RM10,000
The limit will apply to visitors and tourists in Langkawi and Labuan, subject to a minimum stay of 48 hours.
54. Local film and theatre tickets exempted from entertainment duty
The exemption will apply in the Federal Territories from 2027. State governments have been urged to adopt similar measures.
FOR BUSINESSES AND ENTREPRENEURS
55. RM57 billion in loans and financing guarantees
The total allocation for 2027 will increase from RM50 billion.
56. SJPP and CGC guarantees of up to RM32 billion
The coverage of the Government Guarantee Scheme (SJPP) will be expanded to medium-sized companies across all sectors.
Guarantees of up to RM50 million will be available, with RM1 billion set aside to support local companies' expansion through mergers and acquisitions.
57. RM1 billion in export financing for MSMEs
Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd (BPMB) will provide the financing. The Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) will receive RM60 million to help companies enter and diversify overseas markets.
58. RM30 million MDEC fund to support AI adoption
The fund will help 4,000 MSMEs adopt AI and automate their operations. The programme will also train and certify 5,000 AI professionals.
59. RM450 million for start-ups
The funding will be channelled through Khazanah's Jelawang Capital and the Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP) Pioneer Fund.
60. RM2.1 billion to strengthen mid-tier companies
The funding will cover sectors such as electrical and electronics (E&E), digital technology, aerospace and medical devices.
61. RM270 million to support ECF and P2P financing
The funding will support SMEs, mid-tier companies and social enterprises.
Income tax exemptions for individual equity crowdfunding (ECF) investors and certain angel investors will be extended until the end of 2030.
62. RM50 million UniVC fund
The fund will support the commercialisation of university research.
63. E-Commerce Bill to be tabled
The Bill will be tabled at the next parliamentary sitting to strengthen accountability among online platforms and sellers. Measures to protect MSMEs against unfair competition will also be examined.
64. Improved tax incentives for Global Services Hubs
Effective Jan 1, 2027, the incentives will include a preferential tax rate of 5 per cent for eligible activities. The incentive period may be extended every five years, up to a maximum of 30 years.
65. DE Rantau Nomad Pass extension of up to two years
The extension will be available to existing holders who have reached the two-year limit, subject to conditions.
66. Certain expatriate spouses allowed to work
Effective Jan 1, 2027, the measure will cover spouses holding Dependent Passes whose partners hold Category I Employment Passes, subject to conditions.
67. Tax deductions for Bakat Madani training
The deductions will apply to companies implementing training programmes between June 29, 2026, and Dec 31, 2030.
68. More than RM130 million for the creative industry
The funding will support local films, music and content, including production incentives and additional incentives for works featuring Malaysian culture and national identity.
69. RM935 million for tourism and culture
The allocation includes promotional and event grants.
The scope of the International and Charter Flight Matching Grant will be expanded to include cruise ships, ferries and tour buses bringing international tourists.
70. Incentives for international events
Rebates will be available to event organisers at venues with a capacity of at least 10,000 spectators.
Tax incentives for incentive travel, international conferences and trade exhibitions will be extended until the 2030 year of assessment.
