Title: 2027 Budget drives economic growth through efficient capital formation and mobilisation – SC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget provides strong momentum for the Securities Commission's (SC) efforts to drive economic growth through efficient capital formation and mobilisation, the capital market regulator said.
In a statement, the SC said that the key measures will accelerate the priorities of its Capital Market Masterplan 2026-2030 (CMP), enhancing the vibrancy, inclusivity, sustainability and regional competitiveness of Malaysia's capital market.
Its chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said that the targeted measures and capital market instruments provide the first step in delivering the SC's masterplan in growing the market as well as deepening inclusivity.
"The matching grant for dual listings on Bursa Malaysia and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong will open opportunities for Malaysian companies to access a deeper pool of regional capital and expand beyond our shores," said Faiz.
Guides on a single submission arrangement were recently issued by the SC and Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission, bringing into operation a simplified dual listing framework.
There has also been strong interest from potential Hong Kong fund managers to list Exchange Traded Funds (ETF) on Bursa Malaysia, said Faiz, anticipating the first listing to happen soon.
The Employment Pass facilitation under the Malaysia Asian Business Entity scheme will help eligible public-listed companies attract talent and scale their regional operations across Southeast Asia, he said.
"Together, these measures translate CMP's regional ambition into a clear pathway from accessing regional capital to building a sustained presence regionally," said Faiz.
The enablement of the Multi-Family Office (MFO) model alongside the Single Family Office (SFO) Incentive Scheme also signals that Malaysia is ready to be a full-service wealth management hub for global families and asset owners.
This will further scale the SFO scheme, which collectively has an indicative assets under management of RM20.8 billion to date.
The SC added that the 2027 Budget measures are also key to meeting the SC's CMP target of raising RM90 billion to RM100 billion in sustainable financing by 2030.
It also welcomes the government's continued support to strengthen Malaysia's global leadership in Islamic finance.
"The tax deduction for eligible issuance costs of SC-approved Sukuk PRISMA issuances will support the growth of sustainable Islamic financing while enhancing Malaysia's attractiveness to international investors," said Faiz.
Complementing this, the income tax exemption on grants received under the Sustainable and Responsible Investment (SRI) Sukuk scheme and Bond Grant scheme from Jan 1, 2027 will help reduce issuance costs and encourage greater adoption of sustainable financing solutions.
The extension of the tax incentive for Islamic Fund Management further reinforces Malaysia's competitiveness as a regional Islamic wealth and asset management hub, supporting the continued growth of the Islamic capital market ecosystem, the regulator said.
Meanwhile, the RM270 million allocation for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) will ensure better access to capital for the businesses.
This will be mobilised through Equity Crowdfunding (ECF) and peer-to-peer (P2P) financing platforms, said the SC.
"It expands the range of financing options available to MSMEs, reducing their reliance on traditional funding sources while improving access to growth capital," said Faiz.
The extension of fiscal support for ECF and P2P financing will further strengthen the alternative financing ecosystem, enabling more businesses to secure funding at different stages of their growth journey and fostering a more vibrant entrepreneurial landscape in Malaysia, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia takes legal action against individuals, firms over forest fires
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesia is taking legal action against individuals and corporations over forest and land fires, with 198 suspects identified in 247 police reports, says the Indonesian Embassy in Malaysia.
In a statement today, the embassy said a further 97 police reports involved corporations.
The Environment Ministry had identified 57 business entities across eight provinces, with 33,514.01ha of burned land within concession areas.
Of these, 16 entities in Sumatra accounted for 3,813.85ha, while 41 in Kalimantan accounted for 29,700.16ha.
Separately, the Forestry Ministry had imposed administrative sanctions on 26 legal entities, comprising 25 holders of forest utilisation business licences and one holder of a forest area use approval.
The penalties included revoking five business licences, suspending 13 and issuing written warnings or compulsory restoration orders against eight entities.
"Criminal proceedings are also being pursued against 46 legal subjects. Of these, 17 cases are at the preliminary inquiry stage, while 27 are under formal investigation, involving five corporations and 22 individuals," the statement said.
The government was also stepping up fire prevention, healthcare support and public information efforts.
Measures included expanding peatland rewetting, promoting no-burn land preparation in buffer zones, establishing new Fire Awareness Community Groups and preparing forest and land fire contingency plans for areas in Kalimantan.
The embassy said 555 high-confidence hotspots had been detected through 24-hour monitoring using the Sipongi system, which integrates data from three main satellite sources.
Of these, 336 were detected in Central Kalimantan, 142 in South Sumatra, 48 in West Kalimantan, 28 in South Kalimantan and one in Jambi.
Monitoring also identified 193 active fire spots, with a target suppression area of 748.04 hectares.
"Through the rapid response of the ground and air task forces, approximately 560.60ha, or about 75 per cent of the target area, had been extinguished," the statement said.
The embassy expressed deep concern over the impact of forest and land fires on Malaysia, particularly deteriorating air quality and haze that had disrupted daily activities and posed potential health risks.
It said Indonesian agencies were working around the clock to extinguish fires and minimise transboundary haze.
"The government also welcomes stronger cooperation with Malaysia and friendly countries in addressing forest and land fires and transboundary haze. It remains firmly committed to controlling and addressing forest and land fires.
"The Indonesian representative offices in Malaysia will continue to facilitate communication and information exchange on efforts to address forest and land fires," the statement added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NUTP: Ensure RM69bil education budget reaches schools that need it most
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Spending under the Education Ministry's nearly RM69 billion allocation in the 2027 Budget must be prioritised according to actual needs, particularly school safety and well-being, says the National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP).
Its secretary-general Fouzi Singon said the allocation, the largest among ministries, must be managed transparently and distributed efficiently to deliver meaningful improvements in schools.
"A bigger allocation does not necessarily mean it is sufficient. What matters more is how the funds are managed and distributed – transparently, and with good governance.
"Wastage must be avoided, and spending should be prioritised according to actual needs, particularly critical areas involving the safety and well-being of the school community," he told the New Straits Times.
He said transparency and efficiency were essential given the substantial funding involved, including RM2 billion earmarked for repairs and maintenance across all types of schools.
Fouzi said the allocation should also strengthen school security, rather than focus solely on physical infrastructure upgrades.
He welcomed efforts to upgrade security equipment and install more closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras, but said greater attention should also be given to improving security services at schools.
Security guards, he said, should have broader responsibilities beyond opening and closing school gates and conducting routine patrols.
"Their responsibilities should extend to checking all areas of the school to ensure the premises remain safe," he added.
When tabling the 2027 Budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the Education Ministry would receive the largest allocation, at nearly RM69 billion, up from RM66.2 billion this year, with funding for
school repairs and maintenance
doubled to RM2 billion.
Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) education expert Dr Anuar Ahmad said the substantial allocation was encouraging, but greater clarity was needed on how the funds would be distributed and spent.
"What remains to be seen is how exactly the money will be distributed, what it will be spent on and which education priorities will be pursued in 2027," he said.
Anuar questioned the lack of specific announcements on school safety, saying the issue deserved greater attention.
"I believe school safety deserves particular attention, and it would have been useful to hear whether a specific allocation had been provided to strengthen safety measures in our schools," he said.
He welcomed the increase in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) funding from RM6 billion to RM8 billion, saying it would expand opportunities for students pursuing skills-based education and improve their employment prospects.
He also welcomed increased funding to repair dilapidated schools, stressing that the problem must be addressed urgently to ensure no student was left behind or forced to study in poor conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Guardian: Tax relief to ease family healthcare costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Guardian Malaysia says the 2027 Budget's higher healthcare tax relief will help ease medical costs for households and make essential healthcare more affordable.
Guardian Malaysia welcomed the measures to ease healthcare costs, including an increase in individual tax relief to RM12,000 from RM9,000.
Managing director Priscilla Wu said the measures recognised healthcare affordability as an important part of the cost-of-living issue, alongside tax cuts that could return up to RM1,600 to household budgets.
She said families facing financial pressure might postpone smaller healthcare needs to prioritise immediate living expenses.
"For many Malaysian families, health expenditure begins at home, with everyday health essentials, responsible self-care, and illness prevention," she said.
Wu also welcomed the expansion of tax relief to cover post-natal care services and total parental care expenses, saying the measures would make investing in family health more affordable.
"As the trusted advisor for wellness serving communities across Malaysia, Guardian believes in making everyday healthcare more accessible and affordable supports healthier families while complementing the government's broader efforts to build a more sustainable healthcare system," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil servants praise 2027 Budget's bid to tackle cost-of-living issues
Article:
KUCHING: The special financial assistance of RM1,500 for civil servants and RM750 for government retirees and veterans is expected to help ease the cost-of-living burden, particularly in meeting daily necessities, children's education and family commitments, while also stimulating domestic spending.
Civil servant Joshua Amir Sibat said this was necessary as, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia's (DOSM) Household Expenditure Survey Report 2024, average household consumption expenditure increased from RM5,150 in 2022 to RM5,566 in 2024, a rise of about 8.1 per cent over two years.
"This highlights the need for financial support to help households adjust their spending amid rising living costs.
"From an economic perspective, the assistance has the potential to stimulate domestic consumption when part of the money is spent on goods and services, thereby supporting local business activity," he said.
He said the one-off assistance should be viewed as a complement to more comprehensive measures to safeguard purchasing power, boost productivity and strengthen the people's well-being.
"The value of the assistance is not only in the amount received, but also in its ability to help recipients meet pressing needs without neglecting long-term financial planning."
Meanwhile, retired serviceman Azhar Ishak, 56, said the increase in Special Financial Assistance (BKK) to RM750 in 2027 was a positive development that would help ease the burden on retirees.
He said the assistance had increased by 200 per cent compared with the RM250 received in 2026.
He added that the increase would help retirees meet their daily expenses, particularly amid rising living costs.
"At the very least, it will help ease the burden on us as retirees," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM19.1bil Higher Education allocation must address lecturers' welfare, workload
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Higher Education Ministry's RM19.1 billion allocation under 2027 Budget must translate into improvements in lecturers' welfare and working conditions amid growing academic and administrative demands.
Malaysian Academic Association Congress (MAAC) vice-president II Prof Dr Fauzilah Salleh said the government's commitment to higher education was good, but the success of the allocation should be measured by its impact on university staff and students.
She said greater attention must be given to lecturers' workload, career development and well-being, rather than focusing solely on university rankings and research achievements.
"In pursuing excellence, we must not forget those who form the backbone of universities, namely lecturers and the entire academic community," she told the New Straits Times.
Fauzilah, who is also a principal research fellow at Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin's Islamic Social Finance Research Centre, said lecturers' responsibilities had expanded well beyond teaching.
She said academics were expected to conduct research, publish papers, supervise students, secure grants and undertake community engagement while meeting administrative requirements and university key performance indicators (KPIs).
She urged the government to provide sufficient and sustained research funding while simplifying administrative procedures that could burden researchers.
"We want universities to produce research that benefits society and the country. However, researchers also need adequate and continuous financial support, along with a research management system that is not overly burdensome," she added.
Fauzilah also called for greater attention to students' living costs, graduate employment opportunities and university autonomy.
She hoped academic staff would have a stronger voice in shaping higher education policies, including the planned reforms to the Universities and University Colleges Act (Auku).
"A great university is not merely one that ranks highly internationally, but one that safeguards the welfare of its community, values knowledge and provides opportunities for lecturers and students to develop," she added.
When tabling 2027 Budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced RM19.1 billion for the Higher Education Ministry, including RM800 million to upgrade university facilities and student accommodation.
He also announced an immediate halt to disciplinary proceedings over freedom of expression and peaceful assembly at public universities, alongside plans to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: RM2k minimum wage falls short of workers' needs – MTUC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) has described the RM2,000 minimum wage as insufficient, saying it falls short of the RM3,100 it had sought and the RM3,400 living wage paid to employees of government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs).
MTUC secretary-general Kamarul Baharin Mansor said the wage gap had created a three-tier system among lower-income workers, with differences between minimum wage earners, micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) workers, and those receiving a living wage.
He said exempting MSMEs from the minimum wage requirement would create confusion and discrimination, with workers performing similar jobs paid differently depending on their employers' status.
He added that MSME workers continued to face cost-of-living pressures, warning that failure to address low wages could affect worker morale and public perception.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month when tabling the
2027 Budget
in the Dewan Rakyat today. The new rate will take effect in June 2027, benefiting more than four million workers.
In October 2024, Anwar announced that the
minimum wage
would rise from RM1,500 to RM1,700 a month, effective Feb 1, 2025.
Kamarul expressed concern over mid-level employees with five to 10 years of experience, saying they were disappointed by the lack of mandatory salary adjustments.
"MTUC is calling on the government to use its authority to compel employers to adjust mid-level salaries accordingly," he said.
While welcoming the proposed minimum wage for semi-skilled workers and graduates, he called for a standardised salary structure covering all employment categories, with minimum pay and annual increments for semi-skilled workers, diploma and degree holders, and experienced employees.
Asked whether the RM2,000 minimum wage was sufficient to ease the cost-of-living burden, Kamarul said it would help, but remained inadequate.
"It helps ease the burden for workers to navigate life. We are not ungrateful to the government, but MTUC feels it falls far short of our demand, which was RM3,100," he said.
He said the announcement could give companies time to calculate costs and prepare their salary schedules.
"We expected the minimum wage to increase. We were just waiting for the announcement on how much the increase would be. So, yes, we are thankful," he said.
Meanwhile, SME Association of Malaysia president Dr Chin Chee Seong said businesses should review their cost structures, strengthen cash flow, invest in automation and digitalisation, and improve workforce productivity to remain competitive.
"They should also review their salary structures to retain experienced workers and avoid unnecessary wage pressures.
"Businesses can no longer depend solely on low labour costs to remain competitive. They must focus on efficiency, innovation, and higher-value products and services," he said.
Chin said the government should provide targeted incentives, affordable financing and practical support to help SMEs make the transition.
"SMEs should use the exemption to strengthen their businesses, not to postpone change. Higher wages must come with higher productivity, otherwise both businesses and workers will eventually suffer," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TNB's RM15 bil grid investment to support power reliability, industrial growth -- Solarvest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) RM15 billion investment in the national grid announced in Budget 2027 today addresses a critical priority and need for the infrastructure to support reliable power and industrial expansion, said Solarvest Holdings Bhd.
Solarvest chief executive officer Datuk Davis Chong Chun Shiong said the company would work with TNB to advance smart grids, digital energy management and utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) to meet rising corporate demand under the accelerated Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS).
"Solarvest is dedicated to support the clean energy adoption in these critical economic hubs, from the semiconductor ecosystems in Penang and Kulim Hi-Tech Park (KHTP) in Kedah, to the Automotive Hi-Tech Valley in Perak, and the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven data-centre development in Selangor and Johor.
"By integrating cutting-edge artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) smart grid solutions, we can effectively mitigate grid congestion, maximise intermittent solar integration, and ensure high-reliability power delivery for mission-critical industries," he said in a statement.
Earlier, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Finance Minister, said during Budget 2027's reading that TNB will invest RM15 billion to strengthen the national grid to meet the country's growing electricity demand.
Meanwhile, Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC) president and chief executive officer Mohd Yazid Ja'afar said Budget 2027 would help Malaysian oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) companies strengthen sustainability, develop skills in new energy sectors and expand into global markets.
"The initiatives announced in Budget 2027 open practical doors for future-ready OGSE companies. MPRC will work with the industry to help them walk through those doors.
"Through the OGSE Blueprint and its programmes, MPRC will continue to help Malaysian OGSE companies turn these enabling measures into tangible growth, at home and abroad, as the industry builds a more competitive, resilient and sustainable future," he said in a separate statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil servants to get RM1,500 aid, pensioners RM750 under Budget 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 1.3 million civil servants in Grade Utama B and below, including those on contract appointments, will receive RM1,500 in special financial assistance under Budget 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the finance minister, announced the assistance when tabling the Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
More than one million government pensioners, including pensionable and non-pensionable veterans, will also receive RM750 each.
The payments will be made in two instalments, with disbursements scheduled before Aidilfitri and ahead of the 70th anniversary of Merdeka.
Separately, the government will provide RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel in recognition of their service.
The recipients include KAFA and takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siak, noja and marbut.

Title: Rehda backs Budget 2027 housing measures but calls for more action on rising costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda)
has
welcomed measures in Budget 2027 to support homeownership, while urging the government to do more to address rising development costs and housing affordability.
Its president, Datuk Zaini Yusoff, said in a statement that the expanded stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers would help reduce the upfront cost of buying a home.
Under the measures announced, buyers of properties priced up to RM500,000 would receive full stamp duty exemptions on instruments of transfer and loan agreements.
For properties priced up to RM750,000, the exemption would cover the first RM500,000, with a 50 per cent exemption on the remaining amount.
“These measures will help ease the upfront financial burden of aspiring homeowners,” he said.
Zaini said Rehda hoped the government would continue reviewing the eligibility thresholds in line with prevailing house prices and market conditions, including considering extending the incentives to properties priced up to RM1 million.
The association also welcomed stamp duty exemptions for rehabilitating abandoned housing projects, saying
they
could help revive projects and provide relief to affected purchasers.
It further welcomed RM20 billion in housing financing guarantees under Syarikat Jaminan Kredit Perumahan, which is expected to benefit about 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly those with irregular incomes.
“Improving access to end-financing remains crucial in addressing the challenges
faced by prospective purchasers,”
Zaini said.
Rehda said the government’s continued commitment to affordable housing was also encouraging, with nearly RM1 billion allocated for Rumah Mesra Rakyat and Programme Residensi Rakyat.
It cited affordable housing initiatives by Petronas and the Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil development as further efforts to expand opportunities for Malaysians, particularly lower-income groups.
The association also welcomed the extension until December 31, 2030, of investment tax allowances of up to 100 per cent for qualifying green technology projects and assets.
It said the incentives could encourage more sustainable practices, especially among smaller developers facing higher implementation costs.
However, Rehda remained concerned about rising development
costs, including construction materials, labour and regulatory compliance,
and called for further measures to ease
the
pressure.
“More needs to be done to ensure a more holistic change in housing affordability, such as
the review of
all related charges imposed by the federal and state governments, including infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory and compliance charges.
“These costs remain a challenge in developers’ efforts
in addressing
affordability, and we reaffirm our commitment to engage with the government and all relevant parties to meet this goal,” Zaidi said.
Rehda also urged the government to reconsider reviving the Home Ownership Campaign, particularly to help sell completed but unsold residential properties while giving more Malaysians the opportunity to own a home.
The Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) is a government-supported initiative designed to help more Malaysians buy homes. It has offered incentives such as stamp duty exemptions and developer discounts, while encouraging sales of eligible residential properties.

Title: PLUS to close Bangi Toll Plaza road shoulder for widening works until June 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — PLUS Malaysia Berhad (PLUS) will temporarily close the road shoulder after the exit lane of the Bangi Toll Plaza towards Bandar Baru Bangi from today until June 28 next year to facilitate road widening works.
In a statement today, PLUS said the works were scheduled to take approximately eight months as part of the company’s ongoing efforts to improve highway facilities and enhance users’ comfort.
The closure will only be implemented during off-peak hours, from 10 pm to 5.30 am, to minimise disruption to traffic flow in the area.
Motorists passing through the area are advised to slow down, comply with safety signs and the stipulated speed limits, and follow instructions from personnel at the site.
Users are also advised to plan their journeys and obtain the latest traffic updates through the PLUS app, the company’s official social media platforms, including its X account @plustrafik, and electronic message signs (VMS) at selected locations.
For current traffic information or emergency assistance on the highway, users can contact PLUSLine at 1800-88-0000. — Bernama

Title: E-Commerce Bill to protect small traders, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government will table an E-Commerce Bill at the next parliamentary sitting to strengthen accountability among online platforms and sellers, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the government was urgently examining legislative and enforcement measures to protect micro, small and medium enterprises from unfair competition and ensure goods purchased by consumers were safe.
“The government takes seriously the concerns of small traders over the presence of foreign e-commerce companies entering the domestic market without adequate oversight and enforcement,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
The fifth Madani Budget, themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi”, is the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Home, Defence Ministries each allocated RM22b
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Home Ministry and Defence Ministry have each been allocated RM22 billion under Budget 2027, tabled in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said RM7.1 billion of the total allocation would be channelled to procure and maintain assets for the armed forces, police, and uniformed agencies under the Home Ministry.
He said the government had also agreed to build several new facilities, including the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) Johor headquarters in Tanjung Kupang, the General Operations Force (GOF) 19th Battalion Complex in Cheras, the Keningau Immigration Office in Sabah, and three new police stations in Sungai Rambai, Melaka; Tanjung Malim, Perak; and Batu Lintang, Sri Aman, Sarawak.
“An allocation of RM490 million will be provided to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), while security screening at airports will be tightened, including mandatory drug and alcohol tests for pilots and flight crew.
“A total of 48 new body and baggage scanners will be installed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Penang International Airport and Kota Kinabalu International Airport,” he said when tabling the budget themed “Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground”.
Anwar also said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had blocked more than 5.7 billion scam-related calls and SMS messages.
He said the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) would develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered application to enable the public to check suspicious phone numbers, bank accounts and links before making transactions, allowing scams and cybercrimes to be detected earlier.
“The Royal Malaysia Police’s D11 Division is also strengthening the Malaysia Internet Crime Against Children system, which is equipped with advanced analytical capabilities to detect perpetrators and child sexual exploitation networks at an earlier stage.
“The Safe Internet Campaign will also be intensified in all schools, with a focus on addressing cyberbullying and child exploitation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 draws positive response from ministers over focus on living costs, wages and public services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Budget 2027 has drawn broadly positive reactions from Cabinet ministers, who welcomed its emphasis on easing the cost of living, raising wages and improving public services, as the government seeks to ensure that the benefits of economic growth reach ordinary Malaysians.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the measures reflected public feedback gathered through nationwide engagement sessions, particularly concerns over rising living costs and the need for better wages.
“Our effort in Budget 2027 is to ensure that the spillover gains from the country successfully becoming a strong trading nation are passed down to the people,” he said at a press conference following the budget's tabling in Parliament today.
“The government has listened to feedback received from various parties, through the budget roadshows, engagement sessions, and the grievances brought to us,” he added.
“Today we can see how we outlined our focus areas during the pre-budget sessions to address cost-of-living issues and improve wage quality across the country.”
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, earlier tabled Budget 2027, which places greater emphasis on boosting household disposable income and supporting middle-income earners alongside continued economic reforms.
Among the measures announced were an increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 per month, higher entry-level pay floors for graduates and semi-skilled workers, tax relief for middle-income earners and expanded direct cash assistance programmes.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi welcomed the budget’s focus on technical and vocational education and training (TVET), saying the measures would help address financial pressures faced by the M40 while improving employment prospects for skilled workers.
“Overall, this budget reflects the government’s strong commitment to addressing the problems faced by the M40 group, whose disposable income and purchasing power have been under pressure because of high financial commitments,” he said in his initial reaction.
Zahid said the RM8 billion allocation for TVET would allow the government to expand training in specialised fields, including robotics, and improve workers’ employability.
“We will expand courses that are appropriate to market demand, so that the skills acquired can lead to better employment prospects,” he said, also welcoming provisions for higher wages for skilled workers.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi speaks during a press conference at Parliament in Kuala Lumpur on October 9, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said his ministry had received a slight increase in its allocation to RM12.68 billion, stressing that the priority was to ensure programmes delivered meaningful benefits to target groups.
Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil, meanwhile, welcomed measures to assist the M40 and B40 groups, as well as support for the local film industry and continued investment in digital infrastructure.
“For the first time, the film sector has received interesting support,” he said, expressing hope that Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya would see more filmmaking activity, which could contribute to economic growth and job creation.
Fahmi also highlighted the government's recognition of National Information Dissemination Centres (NADI) and the importance of continued investment in the Jalinan Digital Negara (JENDELA) initiative and submarine cable connectivity.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad described the RM47.7 billion allocation for his ministry as a reasonable basis for continuing healthcare reforms, including addressing longstanding staffing shortages and improving medical facilities.
He welcomed the provision of more than 9,000 permanent positions for contract doctors, as well as increased post-basic incentive payments for 47,000 paramedics and nurses.
Dzulkefly also highlighted RM1.2 billion for maintaining and repairing public hospitals and clinics, saying the additional resources would help the ministry improve healthcare services.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad speaks during a press conference following the tabling of Budget 2027 at Parliament in Kuala Lumpur on October 9, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi welcomed increased funding for infrastructure and smaller contractors, despite his ministry receiving a relatively modest 1.78 per cent increase in its overall allocation.
“What is important is how we use it. We have many programmes and projects,” he said, pointing to additional opportunities for G1 to G4 contractors and RM800 million for construction, roads and infrastructure, including RM350 million for Sabah and Sarawak contractors.
Nanta said allocations for district engineers had increased from RM30 million to RM40 million, allowing smaller infrastructure problems to be addressed more quickly without further approvals.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi (centre) speaks to members of the media during a press conference following the groundbreaking ceremony for the third tunnel and widening project of the Kuala Lumpur-Karak (KLK) Highway at KM36.9 eastbound on August 20, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
He also welcomed provisions for motorcycle shelters, closed-circuit television cameras along PLUS highways and 50 electric vehicle charging points, saying the measures would improve facilities for road users despite government spending constraints.
Beyond the sector-specific allocations, Budget 2027 also increased funding for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM16 billion, from RM15 billion, while raising individual income tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000.
The measures reflect what appears to be a central theme of Anwar’s fifth budget — ensuring that the gains from economic growth and reforms pursued over the past four years translate into higher household incomes, reduced financial pressures and tangible improvements in the daily lives of Malaysians.

Title: Malaysia’s approved investments rise 11.7pc to RM218.5b in first half of 2026, says PM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Malaysia’s approved investments rose 11.7 per cent to RM218.5 billion in the first half of 2026, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, also the finance minister, said Malaysia was on track to reach a new record high for the third consecutive year.
“Government-linked investment companies (GLICs) have been entrusted with building domestic economic resilience and enhancing the capabilities of local companies in high-value sectors.
“For example, Sime Darby Property, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) have established the RM1.25 billion New Economy Venture Fund to develop data centres and logistics assets in Elmina, Selangor,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Meanwhile, he said Khazanah Nasional Bhd and the Retirement Fund (KWAP) had invested RM1.2 billion to help local semiconductor companies move up the value chain. “This includes a collaboration between Khazanah and the Selangor state government on an investment fund for semiconductor development in Selangor,” he added.
The fifth Madani Budget, themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi” (Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground), is the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: RM2.62b aid for paddy farmers, incentives for fishermen, smallholders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is allocating RM2.62 billion in aid to paddy farmers under Budget 2027, covering various subsidies and incentives to increase rice production and safeguard their welfare.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the assistance would enable paddy farmers to receive benefits of about RM4,300 per hectare of paddy field, including subsidies for seeds, fertiliser, pesticides, ploughing costs and paddy prices.
He said the government had agreed to increase the paddy harvesting incentive from RM50 to RM100 per hectare per season, while the ploughing incentive, which had been increased to RM300, would be maintained and extended to paddy farmers in Sabah and Sarawak.
“To rehabilitate and rejuvenate paddy fields, RM20 million will be provided to supply foliar fertiliser for more than 10,000 hectares of paddy fields.
“The Five-Season Padi Cultivation in Two Years Project is crucial to ensuring the continuity of the country’s rice supply, and work to upgrade irrigation systems in 15 paddy field blocks is progressing according to schedule. In addition, the Pedu Dam rehabilitation project in Kedah is expected to be completed by the end of 2027,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
For the fisheries and fishing sector, he said the government would increase the number of special boat licence holders from 17,000 to 20,000 fishermen, with an allocation of RM30 million, while providing aquaculture project grants and RM40 million in financing through Agrobank.
Eligible fishermen will also continue to enjoy subsidised diesel at RM1.65 per litre, while RM178 million will be allocated, among others, for catch incentives and a monthly Cost of Living Allowance of up to RM300.
Anwar said the government had allocated RM300 million to strengthen cooperation with state governments in implementing agrofood projects, in addition to providing more than RM1 billion in financing to agro-entrepreneurs through Agrobank, Bank Rakyat and the Malaysia Cooperative Societies Commission.
For smallholders in the oil palm sector, the government is providing RM100 million in hybrid financing for replanting involving 4,500 smallholders, as well as RM200 million in soft financing, with smallholders bearing only a two per cent interest rate and being granted a four-year repayment deferment.
The allocation for rehabilitating farm roads will also be doubled from RM50 million to RM100 million, while RM30 million will be provided to curb diseases and pest attacks affecting crops, including oil palm, cocoa and pepper.
The government has also agreed to increase the Rubber Production Incentive from RM3 to RM3.30 per kilogramme, which is expected to benefit more than 300,000 rubber smallholders.
Anwar said the government had also approved RM1.26 billion for 2027 to strengthen Felda’s finances, maintain roads and provide housing for the Felda community.
He said the average net income of Felda settlers had increased from RM2,272 per month in 2023 to RM3,800 this year, while 109,000 settlers now held land titles. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: RM8b for TVET, 30,000 new job opportunities via BAKAT Madani
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has allocated RM8 billion for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) across ministries under Budget 2027 to enhance the skills and employability of young people.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was also targeting 30,000 new job opportunities through the BAKAT Madani initiative next year, including through the participation of private companies.
He said the initiative was launched following the commitment of six government-linked investment companies (GLICs), Petronas and the network of government-linked companies (GLCs) to provide training and quality job opportunities for 25,000 youths.
“To encourage greater participation by private companies, tax deductions will be granted to companies implementing BAKAT Madani training programmes from June 29, 2026 to December 31, 2030,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said that under the overall skills development initiative, HRD Corp, with an allocation of RM3 billion, would offer three million skills training opportunities, including for continuing professional development among professionals.
He said the Skills Development Fund Corporation (PTPK) had allocated RM500 million to finance trainees enrolled in skills training programmes at public and private skills training institutes registered with the corporation.
In addition, Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) would train and place 1,000 Bumiputera youths in high-growth sectors, while trainees skilled in electrical wiring at GIATMARA would help repair the wiring in 20,000 homes belonging to poor families.
The Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) would train 10,000 youths in robotics and digital technology to create career opportunities and reduce dependence on foreign labour.
Anwar said ADTEC JTM would provide graduates with a pathway to high-skilled automotive careers through the Advanced Automotive Technology programme, while community colleges would continue to offer short courses to tahfiz students as a pathway to employment, entrepreneurship and higher education.
Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel of other ranks who have completed their service will also be provided with skills training through collaborations with institutions such as the Universiti Kuala Lumpur Malaysian Institute of Aviation Technology (UniKL MIAT) and Akademi Laut Malaysia (ALAM).
Meanwhile, he said the government had increased the allocation for the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (MITRA) to RM150 million, prioritising training and employment opportunities for Indian youths in fields such as industrial automation, technology and aircraft maintenance. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: Registration to open next week for affordable smart city Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced that the affordable housing township Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil will be developed as a residential area complete with amenities, including a vertical school.
During the tabling of Budget 2027 today, he said registration for the first phase of the proposed 17,000-unit housing development will open on Monday.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said nearly RM1 billion has also been allocated for projects under the People-Friendly Homes (Rumah Mesra Rakyat) and People's Residency Programme (Program Residensi Rakyat).
“Four new housing projects will be implemented in Kulai, Johor; Nilai, Negeri Sembilan; Paya Rumput, Melaka; and Lembah Pertang, Terengganu,” he said.
Anwar also announced that the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) will provide housing financing guarantees of up to RM20 billion.
“This guarantee will assist 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly the self-employed who do not have a fixed income,” he said.
The SJKP is a federal government-backed programme under the Finance Ministry designed to help first-time homebuyers — especially those with irregular, non-fixed or informal incomes — secure housing loans from participating banks.

Title: Ringgit gains against US dollar as Budget 2027 underscores fiscal discipline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The ringgit closed higher against the US dollar today, supported by the government’s commitment to fiscal consolidation under Budget 2027, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the ringgit climbed to 4.0830/0875 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0890/0940.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Malaysia’s fiscal deficit is expected to narrow to 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) next year from an estimated 3.6 per cent in 2026. “The expected narrowing of the fiscal deficit suggests that the government remains committed to fiscal discipline, which can effectively help bolster confidence among traders and investors towards the ringgit,” he told Bernama today.
At the close, the ringgit traded mixed against a basket of major and ASEAN currencies.
The local note rose against the Japanese yen to 2.5791/5821 from 2.5834/5867 at yesterday’s close, but dipped against the British pound to 5.4063/4123 from 5.3930/3996 and eased against the euro to 4.5807/5858 from 4.5719/5775 previously.
