Title: Budget 2027: Health minister vows to complete 9,000 contract-to-permanent doctor transitions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Health Ministry (MoH) will complete the process of appointing 9,000 contract doctors to permanent positions throughout 2027, effectively ending the interim contract doctor system, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said.
He said the initiative would require a somewhat different management approach to expedite the appointments while taking into account the stipulated requirements and the respective recruitment groups or cohorts of doctors.
“We will implement this in a way that may be somewhat innovative to ensure it is addressed as soon as possible. This requires some changes in management, explanation and approach. Don’t worry, we will put an end to it in 2027,” he told reporters after the tabling of Budget 2027 in Parliament today.
When tabling the budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that more than 9,000 contract doctors would be offered permanent positions next year, while doctors who complete their housemanship in the future would be offered permanent posts as medical officers.
Anwar also said that since 2023, the Madani Government had appointed more than 15,000 contract doctors to permanent positions, including 4,000 this year.
Asked whether the initiative could resolve the shortage of doctors, Dzulkefly described it as a positive step that could help address the healthcare workforce challenges faced by the ministry, particularly this year.
He said the RM47.7 billion allocated to the ministry under Budget 2027 comprised RM40.95 billion for operating expenditure and RM6.75 billion for development, enabling it to continue its healthcare reform agenda.
Among the initiatives to strengthen the healthcare workforce was an increase in the Post-Basic Incentive Payment from RM100 to RM200 a month, benefiting 47,000 paramedics and nurses, as well as an increase in the Air Health Services Incentive Payment from RM30 to RM100.
On healthcare services in remote areas, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, Dzulkefly said MoH would continue to strengthen service delivery in line with the goal of Universal Health Coverage (UHC), ensuring that no one was left behind.
On a proposal for the ministry to own helicopters for air medical services, he said it preferred leasing them as this was more cost-effective and would spare the ministry the burden of maintaining the assets.
Asked whether the country’s healthcare facilities were under pressure due to the haze, Dzulkefly said ministry facilities remained capable of handling the increase in cases related to air pollution, although respiratory cases had risen significantly.
He advised the public to avoid outdoor activities, particularly when Air Pollutant Index (API) readings exceeded 160 or 200, and to minimise exposure to polluted air, especially among children, the elderly and those with pre-existing medical conditions. — Bernama

Title: ‘Today is for the rakyat, tomorrow is for the wife’: Syed Saddiq’s Budget 2027 reply amuses social media
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Muar Member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman left local social media users amused following his response to a post on Threads.
The 34-year-old, who was present at today’s tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Parliament, caught the attention of a Threads user who praised him for finding the time to attend despite his wedding ceremony taking place tomorrow.
“Today is for the rakyat, tomorrow is for the wife. (I) need to show up for both,” Syed Saddiq wrote in response to the post.
His response garnered over 170,000 views with over 12,000 likes along with comments from social media users amused by his choice of words.
https://www.threads.com/@syedsaddiq/post/DeRMNJelDwS
“He mentions ‘wife’ referring to someone else but I’m the one who’s feeling the butterflies,” commented user bloombae.byainawanie.
“From fiancée, to future wife to now just wife, so cute,” commented user nadhrahy_.
“Wow, after this we will be hearing the word ‘wife’ more often,” user sue_saraana96 commented.
Apart from local social media users, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul was also heard wishing “
Selamat Pengantin Baru Muar
” (“Congratulations on your wedding, Muar”) at the end of the Budget 2027 tabling, referring to Syed Saddiq’s constituency.
Tomorrow will mark the main wedding ceremony between Syed Saddiq and singer-actress Bella Astillah, which will take place at the 118th floor of the Merdeka 118.
A special dinner reception will follow on October 18 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec).
The couple also announced two public wedding receptions, dubbed Kenduri Rakyat (people’s feast), in Muar, Johor, on October 25 and Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on October 31.
The couple invited members of the public to share in their happiness.

Title: Sabah, with RM18.6b in allocations, hails 2027 budget as alleviating burden for all Malaysians
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 9 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described the National 2027 Budget as a comprehensive budget that alleviates the people's financial burden and reflects the strength of the country's economy.
He said the budget that was proposed earlier today saw benefitted Malaysians through tax reductions and incentives for civil servants, businesses and all segments of society.
“It demonstrates the strength of our country's economy and financial position, despite the impact of the ongoing crisis in West Asia,” he said after watching the live broadcast of the tabling of the National 2027 Budget at Menara Kinabalu today.
In Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s proposed budget, Sabah continues to be the biggest recipient of federal allocations with RM18.6 billion for next year, an increase of 6.25 per cent compared to RM17.6 billion for this year.
In addition, Anwar said road projects in Sabah and Sarawak would continue with an allocation of RM3.3 billion under the 2027 Budget.
He also announced that the government had agreed to double the number of Public Service Department (JPA) scholarships offered to students from Sabah and Sarawak.
“This means that 4,200 students from Sabah and Sarawak will have the opportunity to pursue higher education at universities each year,” he said.
On boosting power supply system, he said the government has also agreed to install Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) systems at the Dam Road and Segaliud Main Intake Substations at a cost of RM204 million.
The Southern Link Transmission Line project will also proceed as a long-term measure to ensure the sustainability of electricity supply in Sabah.
Road infrastructure along the borders of Sabah, Sarawak and Kalimantan will also continue to be upgraded to facilitate two-way movement.
Anwar also reiterated that the resolution of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) with the two east Malaysian state was to be viewed as part of the national covenant and promised that the interim payment of RM1.5 billion will be settled before the end of the year, while negotiations with Sabah and Sarawak will continue to finalise a fair and sustainable annual formula.
Also watching the live telecast with Hajiji were Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, assistant ministers and senior state government officers.

Title: Lim Guan Eng calls Budget 2027 Anwar’s ‘most reform-minded’ yet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today described Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth Madani Budget as the “most reform-minded” budget yet.
Lim, who is also Bagan MP, said expanding the social safety net to gig workers, persons with disabilities and senior citizens, providing more inclusive funding allocations and adjusting personal income tax rates to address past injustices were steps in the right direction.
“These initial steps of budgetary reforms give hope that there will be more future substantial meaningful reforms in the pipeline that will contain cost of living increases, creating sustainable economic growth especially for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and generating prosperity for all by ensuring that there is more money to spend for Malaysian households,” he said in a statement on Facebook.
Still, Lim said more needed to be done, particularly by allocating 10 per cent of total Bumiputera allocations to non-Bumiputera communities without reducing existing Bumiputera funding.
He said this would ensure a fairer and more equitable distribution of taxpayers’ money to non-Bumiputera communities, which he claimed previous governments had neglected.
Earlier, Anwar tabled the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat, outlining the government’s spending plans and direction for the coming year.
Themed “Malaysia Madani:
Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi
(Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground),” Budget 2027 is the second Budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (RMK13), which serves as the national development framework for the 2026-2030 period.

Title: Budget 2027: Medical groups hail end to contract doctor system, enhanced public-private synergy but seek more on retention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Healthcare stakeholders had mixed responses to the national health allocations announced in Budget 2027, with the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) applauding the move to end the contract doctor system while highlighting critical gaps in workforce retention
The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM), meanwhile, welcomed measures to boost public-private cooperation.
The Ministry of Health’s allocation has increased to RM47.7 billion, from RM46.5 billion in 2026.
MMA president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan described the commitment to end the contract doctor system as a major win for the profession, noting that over 9,000 contract doctors are set to be offered permanent positions in 2027.
“This is a significant milestone and addresses one of MMA’s longstanding calls. We commend the Government for taking this important step towards providing greater job security and career certainty for our young doctors,” he said.
He, however, noted that permanent appointments must be accompanied by a broader strategy to retain healthcare workers.
Malaysia faces a shortage of nearly 11,000 specialists, he said, with demand for specialist care expected to rise amid the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and an ageing population.
“We cannot afford to lose more specialists when we urgently need to train and retain more of them,” he said, calling for greater investment in specialist and subspecialist training, career progression, fair remuneration and better working conditions.
MMA also said more emphasis should be placed on strengthening primary healthcare to tackle NCDs.
The country’s network of private general practitioners remains underutilised and could play a greater role in prevention, early detection and long-term disease management, Sivanaesan said.
“Strengthening primary care is essential to reducing avoidable hospital admissions and easing pressure on specialist services,” he said.
Sivanaesan said the success of Budget 2027 should be measured not only by its allocations, but by improvements in patient care, waiting times, workforce retention and access to healthcare.
MMA reiterated its call for a national healthcare workforce distribution dashboard, providing transparent information on staffing levels and shortages at individual public hospitals and clinics. The data could support workforce planning and help direct resources to areas of greatest need, it said.
The association also noted that the RM1.2 billion allocation for hospital and clinic maintenance was unchanged from 2026, despite ageing facilities and growing maintenance needs.
It called for sufficient funding to address manpower shortages in Sabah and Sarawak, including better incentives and career opportunities, and reiterated its call to restore the previous percentage-based Regional Incentive Payment.
Meanwhile, APHM president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh welcomed measures to reduce patient waiting times, including a RM200 million allocation for outsourcing patients to other hospitals and expanded sessional arrangements for private-sector specialists, with the maximum engagement period extended.
APHM also welcomed Budget 2027’s reflection of work on billing transparency, saying it looked forward to further discussions with stakeholders on implementation.
Dr Kuljit said the e-CKAPS portal, which is due to enable private healthcare facilities to be licensed entirely online from 2027, targets a reduction of up to 65 per cent in processing times.
He said faster licensing could also support Malaysia’s medical tourism sector.
“What matters most is not the size of the budget increase but the outcome for patients.
“APHM stands ready to work closely with the Health Ministry and other stakeholders to turn these measures into real improvements on the ground,” he said.

Title: Four injured after lorry crashes into 11 vehicles in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 9 — Four people were injured in an accident involving a lorry and 11 other vehicles at Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Alam Budiman here today.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department was informed of the crash at about 4.30pm and immediately dispatched personnel to the scene.
“The accident left a man and a woman with serious head injuries, while two other male victims sustained minor injuries,” he said in a statement.
Ashrul said all the victims were rushed to hospital for further treatment.
Earlier, a video of the incident went viral on social media, showing a lorry believed to have been travelling against the flow of traffic before crashing into several vehicles at the road junction. — Bernama

Title: MEF welcomes RM2,000 minimum wage, says MSME exemption gives smaller firms breathing room
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) today welcomed the federal government’s decision to raise the national minimum wage to RM2,000 while exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of less than RM50 million.
The new rate, effective June 2027, was announced earlier by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of Budget 2027.
MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said a balanced approach was essential to ensure efforts to improve workers’ welfare did not inadvertently undermine business viability, discourage hiring or put existing jobs at risk.
“Providing employers until June 2027 is a sensible step that gives businesses the time to plan, adapt and prepare for implementation while minimising disruption to employment and business operations.
“MEF believes that a reasonable transition period, combined with appropriate support for MSMEs, will help ensure that the objective of improving workers’ incomes can be pursued alongside business sustainability and job security,” he said in a statement.
Explaining further, Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy focuses not only on the extent of wage increases but also on ensuring businesses can sustain those wages, protect existing jobs and continue creating new employment opportunities.
He also noted that while the minimum wage establishes the statutory wage floor, it should not be the ceiling for employers who can afford to pay more.
“MEF encourages employers to reward employees in line with their business performance, productivity, skills and contributions.
“At the same time, we must recognise that businesses have different financial capacities, particularly among MSMEs.
“The ultimate objective is to build sustainable businesses that can continuously create quality jobs and provide better wages for Malaysian workers,” he said.
Regarding the MSME exemption, Syed Hussain said such measures reflect an important recognition that wage policies must account for the differing financial capacities of businesses, particularly smaller enterprises that operate with tighter margins and limited resources.
“While larger businesses may have greater financial capacity to absorb higher labour costs, smaller enterprises often face more significant constraints arising from rising operating expenses, limited access to financing, productivity gaps and the challenges of adopting new technologies.
“An exemption for eligible MSMEs would provide these businesses with greater flexibility to strengthen their financial positions, improve productivity and prepare for future wage adjustments without compromising their ability to sustain employment,” he said.
Nevertheless, Syed Hussain said any exemption should be supported by clear eligibility criteria, transparent implementation guidelines and adequate communication to employers and employees.
This includes clarification on how the annual sales threshold of RM50 million will be assessed, the treatment of related companies and the application of the exemption to different business structures.
He said MEF also proposed that the federal government strengthen complementary measures to help businesses improve productivity and pay higher wages over the longer term.
These include targeted productivity incentives, support for digitalisation and automation, skills development and measures to reduce the cost of doing business, particularly for MSMEs.

Title: Haze: 36 areas record unhealthy API readings, Pasir Gudang highest at 190
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 36 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.45pm today, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 190.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas in Johor that recorded unhealthy API readings were Segamat (187), Larkin (185), Tangkak (183), Batu Pahat (177), Kluang (176), Pengerang (175) and Kota Tinggi (175).
In Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Seremban (189), Nilai (183) and Port Dickson (174), while in Melaka, the affected areas were Bukit Rambai (187), Bandaraya Melaka (183) and Alor Gajah (181).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded the highest API reading at 181, followed by Shah Alam (175), Petaling Jaya (167), Klang (167), Banting (166) and Kuala Selangor (156).
Cheras and Batu Muda in the capital recorded readings of 177 and 172, respectively, while Putrajaya recorded 170.
Five areas in Perak also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Tasek Ipoh (182), Pegoh Ipoh (176), Tanjung Malim (174), Seri Manjung (158) and Taiping (110).
Other affected areas were Rompin (162), Indera Mahkota in Kuantan (158) and Temerloh (156) in Pahang, while in Kedah, Sungai Petani (156) and Alor Setar (152) were affected.
In addition, three areas in Penang also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Minden (154), Seberang Jaya (147) and Seberang Perai (129).
A total of 32 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good readings.
API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are considered hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Government-owned Entities Bill to be drafted next year, RM1.1b for enforcement agencies’ operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Enforcement agencies, including the police and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), will receive RM1.1 billion to strengthen their operations under Budget 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Finance Minister, made the announcement while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.
The government, he said, will also draft a new Government-Owned Entities Act to strengthen good governance in government-owned companies and statutory bodies and prevent major financial scandals such as 1MDB and the mismanagement of Tabung Haji and Felda from recurring.
“With the Government Procurement Act coming to force starting 2027, the government will improve transparency and publish project details, including the contractors and contract value,” Anwar said.
“When governance is corrected, the benefits resulting from the change will contribute to the people’s welfare,” he added.
Anwar also said revenue generated from loan repayments, including from education and business loans, disbursed to federal statutory bodies must only be used for the approved purposes and target groups. This, he said, also applies to interests collected from such loans.
He also singled out the reforms that his administration has achieved since coming to power in 2022, including abolishing mandatory death penalty and penalties for suicide and enacting the Online Safety Act and the Anti-Bullying Act.
“Clearly, the hardest change is the reforms to limit one’s own powers,” he said, referring to the ongoing efforts to secure a two-thirds majority to cap a prime minister’s tenure to two terms.

Title: Budget 2027: Bumiputera contractor procurement nearly doubles to RM7.5b, GLICs to invest RM2b
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is set to increase the procurement allocation for Bumiputera contractors in the G1 to G4 grades to RM7.5 billion under Budget 2027, an increase from RM4 billion this year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this follows recent concerns raised by Bumiputera contractors and companies.
“For maintenance, repair and upgrading works of government facilities, the procurement threshold for direct appointment is allowed up to RM200,000 and for quotations, up to RM3 million,” he said.
He added that the Unit Peneraju Agenda Bumiputera (Teraju), a strategic agency under the Prime Minister’s Department, will provide financing of up to RM1 billion while effectively monitoring Bumiputera projects across the country.
Meanwhile, financing funds by Perbadanan Usahawan Nasional Berhad (PUNB) will increase from RM350 million previously to RM500 million.
“The government is providing a stamp duty facility of only RM10 for loan and financing agreements under the Cakna II Scheme, which will be introduced from January 1, 2027to December 31, 2030.
“The same facility will also be extended for the Cakna I Scheme until December 31, 2030,” Anwar said.
Government-linked companies (GLCs) and Petronas are targeting RM58 billion procurement from Bumiputera companies while GLC procurement guidelines — which have not been reviewed since 2006 — will be updated next year.
Anwar also announced that government-linked investment companies (GLICs) such as Ekuinas and PHB will also invest RM2 billion to further empower Bumiputera companies while Khazanah Nasional Berhad and Teraju will be introducing the RM250 million
Dana Ciptawan
(Innovators Fund) to support the growth of mid-tier Bumiputera companies.
“Centralised solar parks for government buildings will be developed with an investment of RM1.5 billion.
“This also provides opportunities for Bumiputera construction, engineering, and maintenance companies.
“Through the LSS6 solar project, 150 megawatts is allocated specifically to Bumiputera companies to support them in the clean energy industry,” Anwar said.
He added that the government is also extending the 10 Bumiputera Champions initiative with an allocation of RM40 million to foster 15 potential companies by 2027.

Title: Budget 2027: Government earmarks RM60m for Matrade, RM1b to boost MSME exports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 - The federal government will allocate RM60 million to the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) to help build local companies’ capacity to enter and diversify their overseas markets, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
In his Budget 2027 speech, Anwar said Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Berhad (BPMB) will also prepare RM1 billion to support local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to explore the export market.
Anwar said the federal government together with the civil servants’ pension fund KWAP will set up a RM50 million UNIVC fund to bring universities’ research to the market, and added that the government will also bear the preliminary risk to enable more private capital to support local inventions.
He said the federal government will also allocate RM142 million for the NADI platform which has enabled many young entrepreneurs to benefit from e-commerce, pointing out that coffee entrepreneur Azmi Warisan from Kampung Sungai Leman, Selangor had successfully increased his revenue by 80 per cent or RM240,000 after using the Nadi platform.
He said JOM Malaysia will also have RM10 million to bring rural products and high-value services to digital platforms and overseas markets.
In support of the low-altitude economy such as those involving drones, Anwar said the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) will invest RM50 million to develop a digital system to manage airspace, national testing site and safety standards.

Title: Budget 2027: Govt rolls out six initiatives to attract global firms, skilled talent
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today the federal government will roll out several initiatives in 2027 to make it easier for global companies to operate in Malaysia and attract top skilled talent.
Tabling Budget 2027, Anwar outlined six initiatives to improve Malaysia’s business environment and competitiveness, amid renewed investor confidence in recent years.
“Reformasi Madani has helped restore investor confidence, with Malaysia rising to 15th place in the World Competitiveness Index in two years.
“Malaysia is also ranked as the top destination for digital nomads in the Rumavi Global Relocation Index 2026,” he told the Dewan Rakyat here.
Among other measures, Anwar said the existing Global Services Hub (GSH) incentive will be further improved starting January 2027.
GSH is a Malaysian government tax and business initiative administered by the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida).
“New companies under the GSH incentive will enjoy a special five per cent tax rate on income from GSH activities.
“A five per cent tax rate on income exceeding the baseline income of existing Principal Hub or GSH companies will also be provided.
“The GSH incentive period will also be extended in five-year increments, up to a maximum of 30 years,” he said.
GSH companies managing treasury and fund activities will also be exempted from withholding tax on interest payments and stamp duty on intercompany loan agreements, which also extends to activities under the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) package.
Anwar said existing DE Rantau Nomad Pass — Malaysia’s official long-stay digital nomad visa — holders who had reached the two-year limit will be allowed to stay and work remotely in Malaysia for an additional two years, subject to conditions.
Separately, spouses of expatriates holding Category I Employment Passes and Dependant Passes will also be allowed to work in Malaysia, subject to stipulated conditions beginning next year.
“This is aimed at ensuring Malaysia remains an attractive destination for global talent without requiring their spouses to sacrifice their careers,” he said.
Anwar also announced the introduction of the Malaysian Asean Business Entity (MyABE) status to help Malaysian companies develop across Asean.
“The Securities Commission, in collaboration with TalentCorp, will facilitate preliminary Employment Pass applications for listed MyABE companies, with a target processing time of five working days,” he said.
He said the government was also reviewing the Reinvestment Allowance including its eligibility criteria and incentive structure, to make it more targeted and improve industrial competitiveness.
The Reinvestment Allowance is an incentive provided to encourage reinvestment or continued investment by foreign and domestic investors.
Lastly, Anwar said the Securities Commission and Hong Kong regulators would cooperate to facilitate dual listings by Malaysian companies in both markets, providing matching grants to cover listing costs.

Title: Budget 2027: Government halts public university disciplinary proceedings relating to free speech
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has halted disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of speech, expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly with immediate effect.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Higher Education Ministry was preparing a comprehensive legal framework to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), covering university autonomy, academic freedom and student rights.
“With immediate effect, all disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of speech, expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly have been halted,” Anwar told the Parliament today during the tabling of the Budget 2027.
Enacted in 1971, AUKU provides the legal framework for the establishment, administration and governance of public universities. It has long faced criticism over restrictions on student activism and political participation.
The Act was tightened through amendments in 1975 following a wave of student activism, giving university authorities greater powers over student activities and disciplinary action.
Subsequent amendments relaxed some restrictions. Changes in 2012 allowed students to participate in political party activities outside campus, while amendments in 2024 transferred disciplinary decisions involving public university students from vice-chancellors to student disciplinary committees.
Despite these changes, student groups continued to call for the Act’s repeal, arguing that it restricted student freedom and participation in public affairs.
Anwar announced in August that the government would repeal AUKU, assuring students that the move would not be followed by new laws that similarly restrict student movements.
The Higher Education Ministry subsequently announced that disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of expression, public criticism and peaceful assembly would be stopped immediately while work on the new legal framework continued.
However, the ministry said cases involving violence, vandalism, criminal offences, academic misconduct and breaches of legitimate disciplinary rules would remain subject to existing laws and regulations.

Title: Anwar: Voluntary medical insurance MediAsas to kick off in 2027, EPF Akaun Sejahtera can pay premiums
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — MediAsas, a voluntary medical insurance and takaful plan, will be launched nationwide at affordable prices in January 2027, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
While tabling Budget 2027 at Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said MediAsas would help keep hospital bills under control and more predictable according to diagnosis type.
“Starting 2027, private hospital bills must use a standard and transparent category of charges so that patients understand what they are paying and to reduce price distortions,” he said.
Anwar also said Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributors under 55 years old can also tap into their Akaun Sejahtera to pay for MediAsas premiums.
The government will also extend a subsidy of RM200 per worker for MediAsas premiums for a maximum of 50 employees during the first year for small- and medium-sized enterprises comprising less than 75 employees.
Anwar also said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will continue implementing the electronic medical records system in all public healthcare facilities nationwide with a RM1 billion allocation.

Title: Budget 2027: Higher Education Ministry gets RM19.1bil, RM800mil for university facilities upgrades
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Higher Education Ministry will receive RM19.1 billion under Budget 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this will include RM800 million to upgrade university facilities and replace ageing equipment.
“The allocation would be used to improve infrastructure such as lecture halls and student accommodation, as well as replace outdated equipment,” Anwar told the Parliament today.
A slight increase from the Budget 2026 allocation of 18.6 billion, the Budget 2027 allocation follows a broader expansion of the ministry’s responsibilities, with Form Six and matriculation students set to come under its purview from 2027, bringing pre-university education within the higher education system.
“The government also welcomes and encourage contributions from the public, alumni and the corporate sector to public universities.
“Donations to public universities would qualify for income tax deductions of up to 10 per cent of aggregate income,” Anwar said.

Title: Budget 2027: Duty‑free shopping limit in Langkawi and Labuan raised to RM10,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The duty-free shopping limit for visitors and tourists in Langkawi and Labuan is set to increase to RM10,000 to boost tourism on the two duty-free islands, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced.
However, Anwar said visitors and tourists must stay for at least 48 hours to enjoy the higher duty-free shopping limit.
“More locally made products from Langkawi will also be exempted from import duties to support local entrepreneurs,” he said.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said this when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Addressing difficulties faced by residents and tourists in finding automated teller machines (ATMs) on some resort islands, Anwar said the government will expand QR code payments to 15 locations next year, including resort islands.
He said small traders often miss out on sales when customers did not have cash.
Anwar further announced that government has also extended the Visit Malaysia campaign until next year, with RM935 million allocated for tourism and culture.
He said among the initiatives under the Visit Malaysia campaign are the provision of incentive grants to tourism industry players to promote and organise tourism events.
“The government will also improve the quality of tourism facilities, including jetty infrastructure and heritage sites with the potential to be recognised by Unesco.
“These include Danum Valley in Sabah, Bujang Valley in Kedah and Taman Negara Pahang,” he said.
Anwar also said arts, culture and heritage will continue to receive support through the organisation of a Cultural Festival in conjunction with the SEA Games.
“The government will also support cultural and heritage industry players, including those involved in handicrafts, weaving and batik,” he said.
To improve international connectivity, Anwar said a Matching Grant for International and Charter Flights will be provided to establish new direct flight routes from China, India, Central Asia and Europe.
Anwar said the grant’s scope will be expanded to include cruise ships, ferries and tour buses bringing international tourists to Malaysia.
He also pointed out that Malaysia must become a preferred destination for major international events.
“To attract more such events, rebates will be offered to organisers holding events at venues with a capacity of at least 10,000 spectators.
“Tax incentives for international-standard incentive travel, conferences and trade exhibitions will also be extended until the 2030 year of assessment,” he said.

Title: Budget 2027: e-ART to be main urban public transport solution in Johor Bahru ahead of RTS Link
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The federal government today said the Elevated Autonomous Rapid Transit (e-ART) system would be the main solution for easing traffic congestion in Johor Bahru.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would also add bus routes, increase bus and KTM Komuter service frequency, and provide Grab shuttle services in high-demand areas ahead of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link opening next year.
“Traffic congestion in Johor Bahru must be addressed immediately.
“Therefore, the government has agreed to implement the e-ART as the main solution,” he said while tabling Budget 2027 at theDewan Rakyat today.
Anwar said the measure is aimed at improving public transport connectivity and easing traffic congestion as cross-border travel between Johor Bahru and Singapore prepares for a major boost with the RTS Link.
On October 2, the Malaysian and Singaporean governments said Passenger service on the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link is now expected to begin in February 2027.
In a joint statement, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Singapore Grantor) and the Ministry of Transport Malaysia (Malaysia Grantor) said they had been informed by RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) of the revised timeline.

Title: Budget 2027: Entertainment duty exemption for local film, theatre tickets in Federal Territories, creative sector gets RM130m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Tickets for local films and theatre performances in the Federal Territories will be fully exempt from entertainment duty starting in 2027, as part of the government’s efforts to support the local creative industry.
The government will allocate more than RM130 million to support the film, music and creative content sectors, aimed at enhancing Malaysia’s image, creating jobs and bringing local stories to the international stage, according to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.
This includes incentives for local and international film and animation productions that shoot in Malaysia, as well as additional incentives for works that showcase Malaysian culture and national identity.
The government will also strengthen the local animation ecosystem to develop 20 new intellectual properties (IPs) and commercialise Malaysian characters globally.
The government also called on state administrations to introduce similar entertainment duty exemptions to support local creative practitioners.

Title: Budget 2027: Form Six students to receive RM2,500 allowance, early school aid increases to RM200 per pupil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Form Six students will receive a RM2,500 cost-of-living allowance each next year, matching the rate given to matriculation students, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
Speaking during the tabling of Budget 2027 in Parliament, Anwar said the assistance would benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide.
Anwar also announced that the government would increase Bantuan Awal Persekolahan (BAP), or early schooling assistance, from RM150 to RM200 per pupil next year.
He said the RM1 billion allocation would benefit 5.3 million pupils, with a family of four school-going children receiving RM800 to prepare for the 2027 school session.
“The assistance will be distributed through schools.
“This arrangement would allow parents to meet their children’s teachers in person and reinforce their shared responsibility for pupils’ academic progress and character development,” Anwar said.
The government will also allocate RM870 million for the Supplementary Food Programme (Rancangan Makanan Tambahan), benefiting more than 800,000 pupils.
Anwar said the government would also improve the School Public Donations Fund (Tabung Sumbangan Wang Awam Sekolah) to allow voluntary contributions from parents, alumni and the public to be used for school operations, facility repairs, equipment purchases and student programmes.
Cash contributions to the fund will qualify for tax deductions of up to 10 per cent of aggregate income.
To ease teachers’ administrative workload, the government will expand the recruitment of teaching assistants to 200 primary schools with high pupil enrolment.
“Teachers should return to their task of educating children without being burdened by clerical work,” Anwar said.
Further expansion will take place in phases following an assessment of the programme’s effectiveness.
